nodes.heading: Magistrates' Court Act 1989
nodes.text: Magistrates' Court Act 1989

nodes.heading: Preliminary
nodes.text: Authorised Version incorporating amendments as at 15 April 2026 The Parliament of Victoria enacts as follows:

nodes.heading: Purposes
nodes.text: The main purposes of this Act are—
to establish the Magistrates' Court of Victoria; and
to amend and consolidate for the purposes of the new Court the law relating to the jurisdiction and procedure of Magistrates' Courts; and
to provide for the fair and efficient operation of the Magistrates' Court; and
to abolish inefficient and unnecessary court process and procedures; and
to allow for the Magistrates' Court to be managed in a way that will ensure—
fairness to all parties to court proceedings; and
the prompt resolution of court proceedings; and
that optimum use is made of the Court's resources.

nodes.heading: Commencement
nodes.text: This Act comes into operation on a day or days to be proclaimed.

nodes.heading: process
nodes.text: includes witness summons, charge-sheet, summons to answer to a charge, complaint, warrant to arrest, remand warrant, search warrant, warrant to seize property, enforcement warrant, warrant to imprison, warrant to detain in a youth justice centre, warrant of delivery and any other process by which a proceeding in the Court is commenced;

subject to paragraphs (ca), (dc) and (e), in relation to a criminal proceeding or a class of criminal proceeding, means the mention court that has been nominated by the Chief Magistrate under section 5A for the proceeding or class of proceeding, but in the absence of any such nomination is the mention court that is nearest to—
the place where the offence is alleged to have been committed; or
the place of residence of the accused; and
subject to paragraphs (ca) and (e), in relation to a civil proceeding, means the civil registry court that is nearest to—
the place where the subject-matter of the complaint arose; or
the place of residence of the defendant; and

in relation to a proceeding in respect of which the Specialist Family Violence Court Division has jurisdiction (other than an interim order under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008), means the venue of the Court at which the Specialist Family Violence Court Division may sit and act that the Court determines is the most appropriate venue for the matter, having regard to the following—
the place where the family violence the subject of the proceeding is alleged to have been committed;
the place of residence of the accused, defendant or respondent (within the meaning of the Family Violence Protection Act 2008);
the place of permanent or temporary residence of the person against whom the family violence is alleged to have been committed;
the safety of the parties;
any other considerations the Court thinks relevant; and
in relation to a proceeding for an interim order under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008 or the Personal Safety Intervention Orders Act 2010 means any civil registry court; and
in relation to a proceeding under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008 or the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016, means—
a venue of the Court determined in accordance with paragraph (ca), (d) or (e); or
the civil registry court which the Court determines is the most appropriate venue for the matter, having regard to the following—
the safety of the parties;
the need to prevent disclosure of a party's whereabouts;
the ability of the parties to attend a particular venue of the court, taking into account their places of work, residence or any childcare requirements;
the availability of family violence support services at particular venues of the Court;
the need to manage case flow;
any other considerations the Court thinks relevant; and
in relation to a proceeding under the Personal Safety Intervention Orders Act 2008, means—
a venue of the court determined in accordance with paragraph (d) or (e); or
the civil registry court that the Court determines is the most appropriate venue for the matter, having regard to the following—
the safety of the parties;
the need to prevent disclosure of a party's whereabouts;
the ability of the parties to attend a particular venue of the court, taking into account their places of work, residence or any childcare requirements;
the availability of mediation assessment services at particular venues of the Court;
the need to manage case flow;
any other considerations the Court thinks relevant; and
in relation to a proceeding in respect of which the Assessment and Referral Court List has jurisdiction, means—
a venue of the Court determined in accordance with paragraph (a), (b), (ca) or (d); or
a venue of the Court at which the Assessment and Referral Court List may sit and act;
in relation to a proceeding under Part 4A of the Terrorism (Community Protection) Act 2003 (other than a proceeding in respect of an offence under section 22CU of that Act), means—

the place of residence of the supported person (within the meaning of that Part) or the person in respect of whom it is proposed that the support and engagement order be made (as the case requires); or
the venue of the Court which the Court determines is the most appropriate venue for the matter, having regard to the following—
the administrative and other facilities available at particular venues of the Court;
the ability of the parties to attend a particular venue of the court, taking into account the respondent's (or supported person's) place of work, residence and any childcare requirements;
the need to manage case flow;
any other considerations the Court thinks relevant;
in relation to a proceeding in respect of which the Neighbourhood Justice Division has jurisdiction, means—
a venue of the Court determined in accordance with paragraph (a), (b), (ca) or (d); or
a venue of the Court at which the Neighbourhood Justice Division may sit and act;

another person who is or has been ordinarily a member of the household of the person.
For the purposes of the definition of family

nodes.heading: member
nodes.text: in subsection (1)—
domestic partner of a person means—
a person who is in a registered relationship with the person; or

an adult person to whom the person is not married but with whom the person is in a relationship as a couple where one or each of them provides personal or financial commitment and support of a domestic nature for the material benefit of the other, irrespective of their genders and whether or not they are living under the same roof, but does not include a person who provides domestic support and personal care to the person—
for fee or reward; or
on behalf of another person or an organisation (including a government or government agency, a body corporate or a charitable or benevolent organisation);
parent of a child includes a guardian of the child or a person with whom the child normally or regularly resides;
relative of a person means—
a father, mother, grandfather, grandmother, step-father, step-mother, father-in-law or mother-in-law of the person; or
a son, daughter, grandson, granddaughter, step-son, step-daughter, son-in-law or daughter-in-law of the person; or
a brother, sister, half-brother, half-sister, brother-in-law or sister-in-law of the person; or
an uncle, aunt, uncle-in-law or aunt-in-law of the person; or
a nephew or niece of the person; or
a cousin of the person—and includes, in the case of domestic partners, a person who would be such a relative if the domestic partners were married to each other;
spouse of a person means a person to whom the person is or was married.
For the purposes of the definition of domestic

registered relationship has the same meaning as in the Relationships Act 2008; and

in determining whether persons who are not in a registered relationship are domestic partners of each other, all the circumstances of their relationship are to be taken into account, including any one or more of the matters referred to in section 35(2) of the Relationships Act 2008 as may be relevant in a particular case; and

There shall be a court to be known as the Magistrates' Court of Victoria.
The Court shall consist of the magistrates, the judicial registrars of the court and the registrars of the Court.

nodes.text: The Court has an Industrial Division.

history.raw: S. 4(2A) inserted by No. 83/1992 s. 181(a).

nodes.text: The Industrial Division has such of the powers of the Court as are necessary to enable it to exercise its jurisdiction.

history.raw: S. 4(2B) inserted by No. 83/1992 s. 181(a).

nodes.text: The Court shall be constituted by a magistrate except in the case of any proceeding for which provision is made by any Act or the Rules for the Court to be constituted by a registrar.
Without limiting subsection (3), the Court may be constituted by a judicial registrar in the case of any proceeding for which provision is made by rules of court for—

history.raw: S. 4(3AA) inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 4(2).

nodes.text: the Court to be so constituted; and
the delegation to judicial registrars of powers of the Court to hear and determine the proceeding.
Despite subsection (3), the Industrial Division shall only be constituted by a magistrate who has been assigned to that Division by an Order made by the Governor in Council.

history.raw: S. 4(3A) inserted by No. 83/1992 s. 181(b), amended by Nos 64/1996 s. 25, 36/2007 s. 3(2).

nodes.text: Nothing in subsection (3A) prevents the Industrial Division being constituted by a judicial registrar in accordance with subsection (3AA).

nodes.text: Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, a party to a proceeding in the Industrial Division may appear by a person who is not a legal practitioner if that person is authorised in writing by the party to appear for the party.

history.raw: S. 4(3B) inserted by No. 83/1992 s. 181(b), amended by No. 35/1996 s. 453(Sch. 1 item 53.1).

nodes.text: The Industrial Division must exercise its jurisdiction with the minimum of legal form and technicality.

S. 4A inserted by No. 2/2002 s. 10.

nodes.text: The Court has a Drug Court Division.
The Drug Court Division has such of the powers of the Court as are necessary to enable it to exercise its jurisdiction.
Despite section 4(3), the Drug Court Division shall only be constituted by a magistrate who has been assigned to that Division by the Chief Magistrate by notice published in the Government Gazette.
Nothing in subsection (3) prevents the Drug Court Division being constituted by a judicial registrar in accordance with section 4(3AA).

history.raw: S. 4A(3A) inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 4(4).

nodes.text: Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, the Drug Court Division may only sit and act at a venue of the Court specified by the Chief Magistrate by notice published in the Government Gazette.

The Drug Court Division must exercise its jurisdiction with as little formality and technicality, and with as much expedition, as the requirements of this Act and the Sentencing Act 1991 and the proper consideration of the matters before the Court permit.

nodes.heading: Adjournment of proceeding to Drug Court Division

history.raw: S. 4B inserted by No. 2/2002 s. 10, substituted by No. 36/2007 s. 4.

nodes.text: The Court, at any time before taking a formal plea from the accused in a criminal proceeding that is not in the Drug Court Division, may adjourn the proceeding to the Drug Court Division at that or another venue if—

history.raw: S. 4B(1) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.3(a)).

nodes.text: it appears to the Court that the accused might be eligible for a drug and alcohol treatment order if convicted of the offence by the Drug Court Division; and

the usual place of residence of the accused (if he or she has one) is within a postcode area specified, in relation to the venue at which the Drug Court Division sits and acts, by the Minister by notice published in the Government Gazette; and

history.raw: S. 4B(1)(b) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.3(b)).

nodes.text: the accused consents to the Court doing so.

history.raw: S. 4B(1)(c) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.3(a)).

nodes.text: Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, a venue of the Court to which the proceeding is adjourned under subsection (1) is the proper venue of the Court for the purposes of this Act.

history.raw: S. 4D inserted by No. 27/2002 s. 6.

nodes.text: The Court has a Koori Court Division.
The Koori Court Division has such of the powers of the Court as are necessary to enable it to exercise its jurisdiction.
Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, the Koori Court Division may only sit and act at a venue of the Court specified by the Chief Magistrate by notice published in the Government Gazette.

The Koori Court Division must exercise its jurisdiction with as little formality and technicality, and with as much expedition, as the requirements of this Act and the Sentencing Act 1991 and the proper consideration of the matters before the Court permit.
The Koori Court Division must take steps to ensure that, so far as practicable, any proceeding before it is conducted in a way which it considers will make it comprehensible to—
the accused; and

history.raw: S. 4D(5)(a) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.4).

nodes.text: a family member of the accused; and

history.raw: S. 4D(5)(b) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.4).

nodes.text: any member of the Aboriginal community who is present in court.
Subject to this Act, the regulations and the rules, the Koori Court Division may regulate its own procedure.

nodes.text: The Koori Court Division has—

history.raw: S. 4E inserted by No. 27/2002 s. 6.

nodes.text: the jurisdiction to deal with a proceeding for an offence given to it by section 4F; and

jurisdiction to deal with a contravention of a sentence imposed by it (including any offence constituted by such a contravention) or variation of such a sentence, in the circumstances set out in section 4EA; and

history.raw: S. 4E(b) amended by Nos 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.5), 26/2012 s. 22(1).

nodes.text: jurisdiction to deal with a contravention of a sentence imposed by the Magistrates' Court (including any offence constituted by such a contravention), or variation of such a sentence, in the circumstances set out in section 4EA; and

history.raw: S. 4E(ba) inserted by No. 26/2012 s. 22(2).

nodes.text: any other jurisdiction given to it by or under this or any other Act.

nodes.heading: Circumstances in which Koori Court Division may deal with contravention of a sentence imposed by another Division of the Magistrates' Court
nodes.text: For the purposes of sections 4E(b) and (ba), the circumstances are—

history.raw: S. 4EA inserted by No. 26/2012 s. 23.
S. 4EA (b)(ii)(iii) repealed by No. 19/2017 s. 50(2).

nodes.text: the accused is Aboriginal; and
the offence to which the sentence relates is within the jurisdiction of the Magistrates' Court, other than—
a sexual offence as defined in section 6B(1) of the Sentencing Act 1991; and

history.raw: S. 4EA(b)(i) amended by No. 19/2017 s. 50(1).

nodes.text: in the case of an offence constituted by a contravention of a sentence referred to in section 4E(b) or (ba), the accused—
intends to plead guilty to the offence; or
pleads guilty to the offence; or
intends to consent to the adjournment, under section 59 of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009, of the proceeding to enable the accused to participate in a diversion program; and
the accused consents to the proceeding being dealt with by the Koori Court Division.

nodes.heading: Circumstances in which Koori Court Division may deal with certain offences

history.raw: S. 4F inserted by No. 27/2002 s. 6.

nodes.text: The Koori Court Division only has jurisdiction to deal with a proceeding for an offence (other than an offence constituted by a contravention of a sentence imposed by it) if—

history.raw: S. 4F(1) amended by Nos 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.6(a)), 26/2012 s. 24.

nodes.text: the accused is Aboriginal; and

history.raw: S. 4F(1)(a) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.6(b)).

nodes.text: the offence is within the jurisdiction of the Magistrates' Court, other than—
a sexual offence as defined in section 6B(1) of the Sentencing Act 1991; and

history.raw: S. 4F(1)(b)(i) amended by No. 19/2017 s. 51(1).

nodes.text: the accused—

history.raw: S. 4F(1)(c) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.6(b)).

nodes.text: intends to plead guilty to the offence; or
pleads guilty to the offence; or

history.raw: S. 4F(1)(b)(ii) substituted by No. 52/2008 s. 252, amended by No. 68/2008 s. 79(a), repealed by No. 19/2017 s. 51(2).

nodes.text: intends to consent to the adjournment, under section 59 of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009, of the proceeding to enable him or her to participate in a diversion program; and

history.raw: S. 4F(1)(b)(iii) inserted by No. 69/2008 s. 79(b), amended by No. 53/2010 s. 221(Sch. item 7.2), repealed by No. 19/2017 s. 51(2).
S. 4F(1)(c)(iii) amended by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(b) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).

nodes.text: the accused consents to the proceeding being dealt with by the Koori Court Division.

history.raw: S. 4F(1)(d) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.6(b)).

nodes.text: Subject to and in accordance with the rules—
a proceeding may be transferred to the Koori Court Division, whether sitting at the same or a different venue; and

the Koori Court Division may transfer a proceeding (including a proceeding transferred to it under paragraph (a)) to the Court, sitting other than as the Koori Court Division, at the same or a different venue.

Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, if a proceeding is transferred from one venue of the Court to another, the transferee venue is the proper venue of the Court for the purposes of this Act.

nodes.heading: Certain matters may be dealt with by Koori Court Division only in certain venues

history.raw: S. 4FA inserted by No. 19/2017 s. 52.

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate may, by notice in the Government Gazette, specify a venue of the court as a venue at which the Koori Court Division may exercise—
the jurisdiction conferred on the Koori Court Division by section 4E(a) in relation to—
a contravention of a family violence intervention order or an offence arising out of the same conduct as that from which the contravention arose; or

a contravention of a personal safety intervention order under the Personal Safety Intervention Orders Act 2010 or an offence arising out of the same conduct as that out of which the contravention arose; and

the jurisdiction conferred on the Koori Court Division by section 4E(b) and (ba) in relation to the contravention or variation of a sentence imposed in relation to a matter referred to in paragraph (a)(i) or (ii); and
the jurisdiction conferred on the Koori Court Division by section 4E(b) and (ba) in relation to an offence constituted by a contravention of a sentence referred to in paragraph (b).
The Koori Court Division must not exercise the jurisdiction referred to in subsection (1) except when sitting at a venue specified under that subsection.

nodes.heading: Sentencing procedure in Koori Court Division

history.raw: S. 4G inserted by No. 27/2002 s. 6.

nodes.text: This section applies to the Koori Court Division when it is considering which sentence to impose on an accused.

history.raw: S. 4G(1) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.7).

nodes.text: The Koori Court Division may consider any oral statement made to it by an Aboriginal elder or respected person.
The Koori Court Division may inform itself in any way it thinks fit, including by considering a report prepared by, or a statement or submission prepared or made to it by, or evidence given to it by—
a Koori Court officer employed as an Aboriginal justice worker; or
a community corrections officer appointed under Part 4 of the Corrections Act 1986; or
a health service provider; or
a victim of the offence; or
a family member of the accused; or

history.raw: S. 4G(3)(e) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.8).

nodes.text: anyone else whom the Koori Court Division considers appropriate.
Nothing in this section affects the requirement to observe the rules of natural justice.
This section does not limit—
any other power conferred on the Court by or under this or any other Act; or

any other specific provision made by or under this or any other Act for the making of any report, statement or submission, or the giving of any evidence, to the Court for the purpose of assisting it in determining sentence.

To avoid doubt, Part 3.10 of the Evidence Act 2008 does not apply to the Koori Court Division in considering the sentence to impose under this section, unless the Koori Court Division directs, in accordance with section 4(2) of the Evidence Act 2008, that it applies.

history.raw: S. 4G(6) inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.1).

nodes.heading: Establishment of Specialist Family Violence Court Division

history.raw: S. 4IA inserted by No. 33/2018 s. 36.

nodes.text: The Court has a Specialist Family Violence Court Division.
The Specialist Family Violence Court Division has such of the powers of the Court as are necessary to enable it to exercise its jurisdiction.

Despite section 4(3), the Specialist Family Violence Court Division may only be constituted by a magistrate who has been assigned to that Division by the Chief Magistrate by notice published in the Government Gazette.
Nothing in subsection (3) prevents the Specialist Family Violence Court Division being constituted by a judicial registrar in accordance with section 4(3AA).

Nothing in subsection (3) prevents the Specialist Family Violence Court Division being constituted by a registrar for the determination of an application under Division 4 of Part 7 of the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016.
In assigning a magistrate, the Chief Magistrate must have regard to the magistrate's relevant knowledge and experience in dealing with matters relating to family violence.

Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, the Specialist Family Violence Court Division may sit and act only at a venue of the Court specified by the Minister by notice published in the Government Gazette.
The Minister must consult the Chief Magistrate before publishing a notice under subsection (7).
Subject to this Act, the regulations and rules, the Specialist Family Violence Court Division may regulate its own procedure.

nodes.heading: Jurisdiction of Specialist Family Violence Court Division

history.raw: S. 4IB inserted by No. 33/2018 s. 36.

nodes.text: The Specialist Family Violence Court Division has jurisdiction to deal with any of the following matters if the matter is within the jurisdiction of the Magistrates' Court and arises from or includes allegations of family violence by a person—
proceedings for or with respect to the following orders under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008—
a family violence intervention order under that Act; or
a counselling order or an order under section 137 of that Act;
proceedings under the Vexatious Proceedings Act 2014 in relation to intervention order legislation within the meaning of that Act;
a proceeding for a declaration under Division 4 of Part 7 of the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016;
civil proceedings for or with respect to damages for personal injury;
matters arising under—
the Family Law Act 1975 of the Commonwealth; or
the Child Support (Assessment) Act 1989 of the Commonwealth;
proceedings for or with respect to the trial of a person for a summary offence or an indictable offence that may be heard and determined summarily;
proceedings for or with respect to the committal for trial of a person for an indictable offence;
proceedings for an order under Division 1 or 2 of Part 4 of the Sentencing Act 1991 that arise from an offence referred to in paragraph (f).
Division 1 of Part 4 of the Sentencing Act 1991 deals with restitution. Division 2 of Part 4 of the Sentencing Act 1991 deals with compensation.
Despite anything to the contrary in the Victims of Crime Assistance Act 1996, if the act of violence to which an application under that Act relates is family violence by a person—
the Specialist Family Violence Court Division has jurisdiction to deal with the application; and
in dealing with the application, the Specialist Family Violence Court Division has the same functions, powers and duties as the Victims of Crime Assistance Tribunal; and

for the purposes of the application and any subsequent review of a decision relating to the application, the Specialist Family Violence Court Division is taken to constitute the Victims of Crime Assistance Tribunal.
The Specialist Family Violence Court Division also has—
jurisdiction to deal with a breach of an order referred to in subsection (1)(a), including any offence constituted by such a breach; and
any other jurisdiction given to it by or under this or any other Act.

Subject to and in accordance with the rules, a proceeding may be transferred to the Specialist Family Violence Court Division, whether sitting at the same or a different venue, but only if the venue where the Specialist Family Violence Court Division is sitting is the proper venue referred to in paragraph (ca) of the definition of proper venue.

Subject to and in accordance with the rules, the Specialist Family Violence Court Division may transfer a proceeding (including a proceeding transferred to it under subsection (4)) to the Court, sitting other than as the Specialist Family Violence Court Division, at the same or a different venue.

Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, if a proceeding is transferred from one venue of the Court to another, the transferee venue is the proper venue of the Court for the purposes of this Act.

history.raw: S. 4J inserted by No. 77/2004 s. 4.

nodes.text: The Specialist Family Violence Court Division may, on its own initiative or on the application of a party to a proceeding, exercise its power under section 128 to adjourn proceedings to give one or more of the parties a reasonable opportunity to obtain legal advice.

The Specialist Family Violence Court Division may resume the proceedings if it is satisfied that the party or parties have had a reasonable opportunity to obtain legal advice whether or not that advice has been obtained.
For party to a proceeding, see section 3(1).

history.raw: S. 4K inserted by No. 77/2004 s. 4.
Notes to s. 4K inserted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.12).

nodes.text: The Specialist Family Violence Court Division may direct that any of the following alternative arrangements be made for the giving of evidence by a witness in a proceeding—
permitting the evidence to be given from a place other than the courtroom by means of closed circuit television or other facilities that enable communication between that place and the courtroom;
using screens to remove the accused, defendant or respondent (within the meaning of the Family Violence Protection Act 2008) from the witness's direct line of vision;

history.raw: S. 4K(1)(b) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.10).

nodes.text: permitting a person to be beside the witness while he or she is giving evidence for the purpose of providing emotional support to him or her;
requiring legal practitioners to be seated while examining or cross-examining the witness;
permitting only persons specified by the Specialist Family Violence Court Division to be present while the witness is giving evidence;
any other alternative arrangements the Specialist Family Violence Court Division considers appropriate.

If the witness is 18 years of age or over, the Specialist Family Violence Court Division may make a direction under subsection (1) on its own initiative or on the application of a party to the proceeding.
If the witness is under 18 years of age, the Specialist Family Violence Court Division must make a direction under subsection (1) unless it considers it is not appropriate to do so having regard to—
the wishes expressed by the witness; and
the age and maturity of the witness; and
any other matters that the Specialist Family Violence Court Division considers relevant.

The Specialist Family Violence Court Division may hear an application under subsection (2) or ascertain the matters in subsection (3) in camera and, except as otherwise directed by the Specialist Family Violence Court Division, persons who are not parties to the proceeding or their legal practitioners or representatives are not permitted to be present while the hearing takes place or the matters are being ascertained.

Any place outside the courtroom where a witness is permitted to give evidence under this section is to be taken to be part of the courtroom while the witness is there for the purpose of giving evidence.
The Specialist Family Violence Court Division may at any time in the course of the proceeding vary or revoke a direction made under subsection

history.raw: Note to s. 4K(6) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.11).

nodes.text: on its own initiative or on the application of a party to the proceeding.
For party to a proceeding, see section 3(1).
If a witness is the complainant in a criminal proceeding, Divisions 4 and 6 of Part 8.2 of Chapter 8 of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009 also apply.

nodes.heading: Restriction on children being called as witnesses or present in court

history.raw: S. 4L inserted by No. 77/2004 s. 4.
Note to s. 4L substituted by No. 52/2008 s. 253(4).

nodes.text: A child must not be present during, or called as a witness in, proceedings in the Specialist Family Violence Court Division, other than proceedings for a family violence intervention order or a proceeding relating to a recognised DVO, if—
the child is a family member of a party to the proceedings; or

history.raw: S. 4L(2)(a) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.13).

nodes.text: the proceedings arise from or include allegations of family violence and the child is a family member of the alleged victim of that family violence.
However, subsection (1) does not apply if—
the child is the accused, defendant or respondent (within the meaning of the Family Violence Protection Act 2008) in the proceedings; or
the Specialist Family Violence Court Division makes an order allowing the child to be present or called as a witness (as the case may be).

For the purposes of subsection (1), a proceeding relating to a recognised DVO is a proceeding for the variation, extension or revocation of a non-local DVO that is a recognised DVO, both within the meaning of the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016.

history.raw: S. 4L(3) inserted by No. 53/2016 s. 106(2).

nodes.text: Sections 67 and 150 of the Family Violence Protection Act 2008 restricts when a child can be present during, or called as a witness in, a proceeding for a family violence intervention order.

history.raw: S. 4M inserted by No. 51/2006 s. 4.

nodes.text: The Court has a Neighbourhood Justice Division.
The Neighbourhood Justice Division has such of the powers of the Court as are necessary to enable it to exercise its jurisdiction.

Despite section 4(3), the Neighbourhood Justice Division shall only be constituted by a magistrate who has been assigned to that Division by the Chief Magistrate by notice published in the Government Gazette.
Nothing in subsection (3) prevents the Neighbourhood Justice Division being constituted by a judicial registrar in accordance with section 4(3AA).

Nothing in subsection (3) prevents the Neighbourhood Justice Division being constituted by a registrar for the determination of an application under Division 4 of Part 7 of the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016.

history.raw: S. 4M(4A) inserted by No. 53/2016 s. 107.

nodes.text: In assigning a magistrate to the Neighbourhood Justice Division, the Chief Magistrate must—
have regard to the magistrate's knowledge of, or experience in the application of, the principles of therapeutic jurisprudence and restorative justice; and
consult with the President of the Children's Court.

The Neighbourhood Justice Division must exercise its jurisdiction with as little formality and technicality, and with as much expedition, as the requirements of this Act and the Sentencing Act 1991 and the proper consideration of the matters before the Court permit.

The Neighbourhood Justice Division must take steps to ensure that, so far as practicable, any proceeding before it is conducted in a way which it considers will make it comprehensible to the parties to the proceeding.
Subject to this Act, the regulations and the rules, the Neighbourhood Justice Division may regulate its own procedure.

nodes.heading: Places where Neighbourhood Justice Division may sit and act
nodes.text: Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, the Neighbourhood Justice Division may only sit and act—

history.raw: S. 4N inserted by No. 51/2006 s. 4.

nodes.text: at a venue of the Court specified by the Chief Magistrate by notice published in the Government Gazette; and
if the Minister specifies a municipal district by notice published in the Government Gazette, at any place within that municipal district.

history.raw: S. 4O inserted by No. 51/2006 s. 4.

nodes.text: In this section—

nodes.heading: close connection
nodes.text: means connection involving regular congregation for the purpose of social or community support;

nodes.heading: municipal district
nodes.text: means a municipal district specified under section 4N(b).
The Neighbourhood Justice Division has the jurisdiction referred to in this section if—

history.raw: S. 4O(2) (ab)(iii) amended by No. 53/2010 s. 221(Sch. item 7.3(b)).

nodes.text: in the case of a criminal proceeding, the accused—

history.raw: S. 4O(2)(a) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.14).

nodes.text: resides in the municipal district; or
is a homeless person who is alleged to have committed the offence in the municipal district; or

is a homeless person who is alleged to have committed the offence outside the municipal district but who is living in the municipal district in accommodation of the kind referred to in paragraph (a) of the definition of

nodes.heading: homeless person
nodes.text: in section 3(1); or
is an Aborigine with a close connection to the municipal district and is alleged to have committed the offence in that district;
in the case of a proceeding under the Personal Safety Intervention Orders Act 2010—

history.raw: S. 4O(2)(ab) inserted by No. 68/2008 s. 80(1), amended by No. 53/2010 s. 221(Sch. item 7.3(a)).

nodes.text: at least one of the parties resides in the municipal district; or
at least one of the parties is—and the Court considers that it is appropriate to deal with the matter in the Neighbourhood Justice Division; or
a homeless person; or
an Aborigine with a close connection to the municipal district—
the whole or a material part of the alleged stalking or prohibited behaviour occurred in the municipal district;
in the case of a civil proceeding or a proceeding under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008 or the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016—
at least one of the parties resides in the municipal district; or
at least one of the parties is—and the Court considers that it is appropriate to deal with the matter in the Neighbourhood Justice Division; or
a homeless person; or
an Aborigine with a close connection to the municipal district—
the whole or a material part of the cause of action or claim arose in the municipal district; or
the whole or a material part of the allegations of family violence occurred in the municipal district.
Subject to subsection (4), the Neighbourhood Justice Division has—
the jurisdiction of the Court given by section 25; and
the jurisdiction given to the Court with respect to a criminal proceeding by or under any other Act; and
jurisdiction to deal with a breach of a sentence imposed by it (including any offence constituted by such a breach) or variation of such a sentence; and

history.raw: S. 4O(3)(c) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.15).

nodes.text: the civil jurisdiction of the Court in respect of a cause of action or claim, or a class of cause of action or claim, or a proceeding, or a class of proceeding, specified in the rules; and
the jurisdiction of the Court given by the Personal Safety Intervention Orders Act 2010; and

history.raw: S. 4O(3)(da) inserted by No. 68/2008 s. 80(3), amended by No. 53/2010 s. 221(Sch. item 7.4).

nodes.text: the jurisdiction of the Court given by the Family Violence Protection Act 2008; and
the jurisdiction of the Court given by Division 4 of Part 7 of the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016; and

history.raw: S. 4O(3)(ea) inserted by No. 53/2016 s. 108(2).

nodes.text: the jurisdiction of the Court given by the Vexatious Proceedings Act 2014 in relation to intervention order legislation within the meaning of that Act.

history.raw: S. 4O(3)(f) inserted by No. 42/2014 s. 106(b).

nodes.text: The Neighbourhood Justice Division does not have jurisdiction to deal with—
a committal proceeding into an indictable offence; or
a proceeding for a sexual offence as defined in section 6B(1) of the Sentencing Act 1991.

history.raw: S. 4P inserted by No. 51/2006 s. 4.

nodes.text: Subject to and in accordance with the rules—
a proceeding may be transferred to the Neighbourhood Justice Division, whether sitting at the same or a different venue; and

the Neighbourhood Justice Division may transfer a proceeding (including a proceeding transferred to it under paragraph (a)) to the Court, sitting other than as the Neighbourhood Justice Division, at the same or a different venue.

Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, if a proceeding is transferred from one venue of the Court to another, the transferee venue is the proper venue of the Court for the purposes of this Act.

nodes.heading: Sentencing procedure in Neighbourhood Justice Division

history.raw: S. 4Q inserted by No. 51/2006 s. 4.
S. 4Q(3) repealed by No. 77/2010 s. 29.

nodes.text: This section applies to the Neighbourhood Justice Division when it is considering which sentence to impose on an accused.

history.raw: S. 4Q(1) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.16).

nodes.text: The Neighbourhood Justice Division may inform itself in any way it thinks fit, including by considering a report prepared by, or a statement or submission prepared or made to it by, or evidence given to it by—
a Neighbourhood Justice officer; or
a community corrections officer appointed under Part 4 of the Corrections Act 1986; or
the Secretary to the Department of Human Services; or
the Secretary to the Department of Health; or

history.raw: S. 4Q(2)(ca) inserted by No. 29/2010 s. 63(2).

nodes.text: a health service provider; or
a community service provider; or
a victim of the offence; or
anyone else whom the Division considers appropriate.
Nothing in this section affects the requirement to observe the rules of natural justice.
This section does not limit—
any other power conferred on the Court by or under this or any other Act; or

any other specific provision made by or under this or any other Act for the making of any report, statement or submission, or the giving of any evidence, to the Court for the purpose of assisting it in determining a sentence.

To avoid doubt, Part 3.10 of the Evidence Act 2008 does not apply to the Neighbourhood Justice Division in considering the sentence to impose under this section, unless the Neighbourhood Justice Division directs, in accordance with section 4(2) of the Evidence Act 2008, that it applies.

history.raw: S. 4Q(6) inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.2).
S. 4R inserted by No. 76/2006 s. 9.

nodes.text: A Sexual Offences List is established.
The Sexual Offences List consists of any proceeding that relates (wholly or partly) to a charge for a sexual offence.
The operation and administration of the Sexual Offences List is at the direction of the Chief Magistrate.
The Chief Magistrate, under section 16A, may issue practice directions, statements or notes for the Court in relation to the Sexual Offences List.
Nothing in this section takes away from, or limits, a discretion or power conferred on the Chief Magistrate by or under this Act.

history.raw: S. 4S inserted by No. 12/2010 s. 5.

nodes.text: An Assessment and Referral Court List is established.
Subject to subsection (3), the Assessment and Referral Court List consists of any criminal proceeding referred to that List by the Court.
The Court must not refer a criminal proceeding to the Assessment and Referral Court List unless—
the accused meets the eligibility criteria specified in section 4T; and
the accused consents to the proceeding being dealt with in the Assessment and Referral Court List; and
the proceeding is at a venue of the Court where the Assessment and Referral Court List operates; and
it appears to the Court that, in all the circumstances, it is appropriate for the proceeding to be dealt with in the Assessment and Referral Court List.

For the purposes of determining whether an accused meets the eligibility criteria specified in section 4T, the Court, so far as is practicable, must have regard to any assessment undertaken by a person with appropriate clinical qualifications and experience in relation to the particular impairment or principal impairment that the accused may have.

history.raw: S. 4S(3A) inserted by No. 23/2012 s. 7(1).

nodes.text: Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, the Assessment and Referral Court List may only sit and act at a venue of the Court specified by the Chief Magistrate by notice published in the Government Gazette.
The operation and administration of the Assessment and Referral Court List is at the direction of the Chief Magistrate.
The Chief Magistrate, under section 16A, may issue practice directions, statements or notes for the Court in relation to the Assessment and Referral Court List.

Without limiting subsection (6), the Chief Magistrate, in exercising the powers under that subsection and having regard to the needs or requirements of persons with different types of impairments, may provide for—

history.raw: S. 4S(6A) inserted by No. 23/2012 s. 7(2).

nodes.text: separate hearing lists within the List; and

history.raw: S. 4S(3)(a) repealed by No. 68/2013 s. 4.

nodes.text: other arrangements to deal with needs or requirements in relation to different types of impairment.
Nothing in this section takes away from, or limits, a discretion or power conferred on the Chief Magistrate by or under this Act.
Nothing in this section or sections 4T to 4Y affects the operation or application of the Crimes (Mental Impairment and Unfitness to be Tried) Act 1997.
A report under section 15(3) must include the following information about the Assessment and Referral Court List—

history.raw: S. 4S(9) inserted by No. 23/2012 s. 7(3).

nodes.text: the source of referral of a proceeding to the List;
the number of persons in each diagnostic criteria who were the subject of a criminal proceeding;
the number of persons who were removed from the Assessment and Referral Court List and the reasons for the removal;
the number of persons who did not complete an individual support plan;
the outcomes of proceedings referred to the Assessment and Referral Court List, including—
the number of accused discharged in accordance with section 4U or 4Y;
the number of referrals to the Assessment and Referral Court List;
the number of accused accepted onto the Assessment and Referral Court List;
the number of proceedings finalised on the Assessment and Referral Court List;
the number of proceedings transferred out of the Assessment and Referral Court List in accordance with section 4X(2);

a summary report of how the Assessment and Referral Court List has functioned, including an assessment, if practicable, of the extent to which the Assessment and Referral Court List reduced re-offending.

history.raw: S. 4T inserted by No. 12/2010 s. 5.

nodes.text: To be eligible for a criminal proceeding to enter the Assessment and Referral Court List, an accused must meet—
the diagnostic criteria; and
the functional criteria; and
the needs criteria.
The diagnostic criteria are that the accused has one or more of the following—
a mental illness;
an intellectual disability;
an acquired brain injury;
autism spectrum disorder;
a neurological impairment, including, but not limited to dementia.
The functional criteria are that the accused has one or more of the diagnostic criteria which causes a substantially reduced capacity in at least one of the following areas—
self-care;
self-management;
social interaction;
communication.

The needs criteria are that the accused would derive benefit from receiving coordinated services in accordance with an individual support plan that has regard to the particular diagnostic and functional criteria as well as all other relevant facts applying to the accused and that may include one or more of the following—

history.raw: S. 4T(4) amended by No. 23/2012 s. 8.

nodes.text: psychological assessment;
welfare services;
health services;
mental health services;
disability services;
drug treatment services or alcohol treatment services;
housing and support services;
other services that aim to reduce the risk of offending or re-offending.

nodes.heading: Specific powers of the Assessment and Referral Court List

history.raw: S. 4U inserted by No. 12/2010 s. 5.

nodes.text: The Assessment and Referral Court List has the powers of the Court necessary to enable it to exercise its jurisdiction.
Without limiting subsection (1), the Court may—
at any time, convene a hearing to receive reports on an accused's progress and compliance with his or her individual support plan;
adjust, amend or vary any individual support plan of an accused;
at any time, remove a criminal proceeding from the Assessment and Referral Court List;
at any time discharge an accused or indicate an intention to discharge the accused.

In hearing any proceeding in the Assessment and Referral Court List, the Court must exercise its jurisdiction with as little formality and technicality, and with as much expedition, as the requirements of this Act and the Sentencing Act 1991 and the proper consideration of the matters before the Court permit.

nodes.heading: Adjournment of proceeding in Assessment and Referral Court List

history.raw: S. 4V inserted by No. 12/2010 s. 5.

nodes.text: The Court, at any time before taking a formal plea from the accused in a criminal proceeding which has been referred to the Assessment and Referral Court List, may adjourn a proceeding in that List for the purposes of a clinical assessment of the accused to—
identify the accused's needs based on the needs criteria set out in section 4T; and

history.raw: S. 4V(3)(a) amended by No. 68/2013 s. 5(1).

nodes.text: prepare an individual support plan for the accused.
The Court must fix a return date for consideration by the Court of the proposed individual support plan.
On the return date, the Court may—
subject to subsection (5), approve the individual support plan, with or without amendments;
fix bail conditions or any undertakings or other conditions the Court considers appropriate;
make any other order the Court thinks fit.
The Court may adjourn a proceeding under this section for a period not exceeding 12 months to enable the accused to be assessed and participate in and complete his or her individual support plan.
The Court must take a formal plea from the accused before approving an individual support plan under subsection (3)(a).

history.raw: S. 4V(5) inserted by No. 68/2013 s. 5(2).

nodes.heading: Other adjournment powers not limited
nodes.text: Nothing in section 4V limits the operation of section 59 or section 331 of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009 in relation to any criminal proceeding.

history.raw: S. 4W inserted by No. 12/2010 s. 5.

nodes.heading: Transfer of proceedings to and from Assessment and Referral Court List

history.raw: S. 4X inserted by No. 12/2010 s. 5.

nodes.text: Subject to and in accordance with this Act and the rules—
a proceeding may be transferred to the Assessment and Referral Court List, whether sitting at the same or a different venue; and
the Court may transfer a proceeding in the Assessment and Referral Court List out of that List and back to the Court for hearing at the same or a different venue.

history.raw: S. 4X(2)(a)(b) repealed by No. 68/2013 s. 6(b).

nodes.text: Despite subsection (1), a proceeding in the Assessment and Referral Court List must be transferred out of the List to a contested hearing in the Court if at any stage the accused pleads not guilty.

history.raw: S. 4X(2) amended by No. 68/2013 s. 6(a).

nodes.text: Despite anything to the contrary in this Act, if a proceeding is transferred from one venue of the Court to another, the transferee venue is the proper venue of the Court for the purposes of this Act.
This section does not limit—
any other power conferred on the Court by or under this or any other Act; or

any other specific provision made by or under this or any other Act for the making of any report, statement or submission, or the giving of any evidence, to the Court for the purpose of assisting it in hearing any criminal proceeding or determining sentence.

nodes.heading: Completion of, and participation in, individual support plan

history.raw: S. 4Y inserted by No. 12/2010 s. 5.

nodes.text: On completion of an individual support plan by an accused to the satisfaction of the Court, the Court must hear and determine the criminal proceeding to which the individual support plan related.
If an accused completes, or participates in, an individual support plan to the satisfaction of the Court, the Court may discharge the accused without any finding of guilt.
The fact of participation in the individual support plan is not to be treated as a finding of guilt.

If the accused is discharged by the Court, the fact of participation in, or completion of, the individual support plan and the discharge of the accused is a defence to a later charge for the same offence or a similar offence arising out of the same circumstances.

If an accused participates in an individual support plan to the satisfaction of the Court and the accused is subsequently found guilty of the charge, the Court must take into account the extent to which the accused participated in the individual support plan when sentencing the accused.

If an accused fails to participate in an individual support plan to the satisfaction of the Court and the accused is subsequently found guilty of the charge, the Court must not take into account the accused's failure to participate in the individual support plan when sentencing the accused.
Nothing in this section affects the requirement to observe the rules of natural justice.
This section does not affect the incurring of demerit points under the Road Safety Act 1986 or regulations made under that Act.
Nothing in this section affects or limits the operation of the Sentencing Act 1991 or the powers of a magistrate or the Court under that Act.

nodes.heading: Where and when Court to be held

nodes.text: The Court is to be held at such places as the Governor in Council, by Order published in the Government Gazette, directs.
The Court may sit and act at any time and place.
The Court must sit on such days and at such times as the Chief Magistrate from time to time directs by notice published in the Government Gazette.

history.raw: S. 5(3) inserted by No. 64/1996 s. 26(2).

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate may from time to time, by notice published in the Government Gazette, alter the days and times appointed for the holding of the Court at any place.

history.raw: S. 5(4) inserted by No. 64/1996 s. 26(2).

nodes.heading: Mention courts
nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate may from time to time, by notice published in the Government Gazette, nominate a venue of the court as a mention court, whether generally or for a particular class of proceeding.

history.raw: S. 5A inserted by No. 64/1996 s. 27.

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate must make arrangements for a magistrate to attend on the day and at the time and place at which the Court is to be held.

If a magistrate does not arrive at the place at which the Court is to be held before the time fixed for the holding of the Court, a registrar may open the Court and adjourn all proceedings to another day or to another venue, as directed by a magistrate.

history.raw: S. 7(1A) inserted by No. 31/2004 s. 4(1), repealed by No. 63/2013 s. 75(1).
S. 7(8) inserted by No. 31/2004 s. 4(3), repealed by No. 63/2013 s. 75(2).

nodes.text: The Governor in Council may appoint as many persons as magistrates as are necessary for transacting the business of the Court.

history.raw: S. 7(1) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 33(1).

nodes.text: Subject to subsection (2B), the Governor in Council may appoint one of the magistrates or, in accordance with subsection (2B), another person to be Chief Magistrate and two or more magistrates to be Deputy Chief Magistrates.

history.raw: S. 7(2) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 33(2).

nodes.text: A Deputy Chief Magistrate appointed on or after the commencement of section 5 of the Courts Legislation (Amendment) Act 2003 holds office for a term not exceeding 5 years specified in the instrument of appointment, but is eligible for reappointment.

history.raw: S. 7(2A) inserted by No. 39/2003 s. 5.

nodes.text: Without limiting subsection (2), the Chief Magistrate, when appointed under subsection (2) must—

history.raw: S. 7(2B) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 33(3), substituted by No. 1/2022 s. 15(1).

nodes.text: already be a Judge of the Supreme Court; or
be simultaneously appointed as Chief Magistrate under subsection (2) and appointed under section 75B of the Constitution Act 1975 as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

history.raw: S. 7(3)(b) substituted by No. 18/2005 s. 18(Sch. 1 item 63.2), amended by No. 17/2014 s. 160(Sch. 2 item 59.2).

nodes.text: A person is not eligible for appointment as a magistrate unless he or she—

history.raw: S. 7(3) substituted by No. 31/2004 s. 4(2).

nodes.text: is or has been a judge or magistrate of—
the High Court of Australia or of a court created by the Parliament of the Commonwealth; or
a court of Victoria or of another State or of the Northern Territory or the Australian Capital Territory; or
is an Australian lawyer of at least 5 years' standing.
A person who has attained the age of 70 years is not eligible to be appointed as a magistrate.

history.raw: S. 7(4) amended by No. 9/1995 s. 10(1)(a).

nodes.text: Every person who is appointed as a magistrate must, before acting as a magistrate, take an oath or affirmation of office in the prescribed form and manner.

history.raw: S. 7(5) amended by No. 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 81.1).

nodes.text: A magistrate may resign from office by delivering to the Governor a signed letter of resignation.
The Chief Magistrate who is a dual commission holder may—

history.raw: S. 7(6A) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 33(4), substituted by No. 1/2022 s. 15(2).

nodes.text: resign simultaneously from both the office of Chief Magistrate under subsection (6) and the office of Judge of the Supreme Court under section 77(4)(e) of the Constitution Act 1975; or
resign from the office of Chief Magistrate under subsection (6) and continue in office as a Judge of the Supreme Court; or
resign from the office of Judge of the Supreme Court under section 77(4)(e) of the Constitution Act 1975 and continue in office as Chief Magistrate without being a dual commission holder.
A magistrate, other than a Chief Magistrate appointed on or after 7 May 1996, is an officer within the meaning of the State Superannuation Act 1988.

history.raw: S. 7(7) amended by No. 13/1999 s. 5.

nodes.text: For the purposes of subsection (7), if any magistrate, other than a Chief Magistrate appointed on or after 7 May 1996, was appointed as a magistrate before the repeal of section 9 by the Courts Legislation Amendment (Reserve Judicial Officers) Act 2013 and immediately before that appointment as a magistrate was an acting magistrate under section 9, during that appointment as an acting magistrate, he or she is an officer within the meaning of the State Superannuation Act 1988.

history.raw: S. 7(7A) inserted by No. 3/2005 s. 10(1), amended by No. 5/2013 s. 32(1).

nodes.text: A magistrate serving under a part-time service arrangement must not engage in legal practice.

history.raw: S. 7(9) inserted by No. 31/2004 s. 4(3), substituted by No. 63/2013 s. 75(3).

nodes.text: Except with the approval of the Chief Magistrate, a magistrate serving under a part-time service arrangement must not undertake paid employment or conduct a business, trade or profession of any kind.

history.raw: S. 7(9A) inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 75(3).

nodes.text: Except with the approval of the Chief Magistrate, a magistrate serving under a part-time service arrangement must not hold an office in any company, trustee company, incorporated association or other entity, whether public or private, in respect of which the magistrate receives remuneration.

history.raw: S. 7(9B) inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 75(3).

nodes.text: Subject to subsection (7A), this section does not apply to a reserve magistrate.

history.raw: S. 7(10) inserted by No. 3/2005 s. 10(2), amended by No. 5/2013 s. 32(2).
S. 7A inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 76.

nodes.text: A magistrate other than an excluded judicial officer may enter into an arrangement with the Chief Magistrate to carry out the duties of magistrate on a part-time basis.
A part-time service arrangement—
must be in writing;
must specify the proportion of full-time duties to be worked by the magistrate to whom the part-time service arrangement applies, which must be a minimum of 0·4 of full-time duties;
may specify an expiry date, but is not required to do so.
The Chief Magistrate may have regard to the following factors in considering whether to enter into a part-time service arrangement—
the operational needs of the court;
the personal and professional circumstances of the magistrate;
parity and equity with other magistrates;
any other relevant consideration.
A part-time service arrangement takes effect from the date agreed by the Chief Magistrate and the magistrate and specified in the part-time service arrangement.

history.raw: S. 7B inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 76.

nodes.text: A part-time service arrangement may be varied by agreement between the magistrate to whom the arrangement applies and the Chief Magistrate.
A variation of a part-time service arrangement—
must be in writing;
must specify the proportion of full-time duties to be worked by the magistrate to whom the part-time service arrangement applies, which must be a minimum of 0·4 of full-time duties.
The Chief Magistrate may have regard to the factors referred to in section 7A(3) in considering whether to vary a part-time service arrangement.

A variation of a part-time service arrangement takes effect from the date agreed by the Chief Magistrate and the magistrate and specified in the written variation of the part-time service arrangement.

history.raw: S. 7C inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 76.

nodes.text: A part-time service arrangement is suspended if the magistrate to whom the part-time service arrangement applies is appointed as any one of the following—
Acting Chief Magistrate;
Acting Deputy Chief Magistrate;
Acting Deputy State Coroner.
A suspension under subsection (1) is for the period of the acting appointment.

history.raw: S. 7D inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 76.

nodes.text: A part-time service arrangement is terminated if the magistrate to whom the part-time service arrangement applies is appointed as any one of the following—
Chief Magistrate;
Deputy Chief Magistrate;

history.raw: S. 7D(1)(b) substituted as s. 7D(1)(c) by No. 21/2015 s. 3(Sch. 1 item 32.2).

nodes.text: Deputy State Coroner.
A part-time service arrangement may be terminated by agreement between the magistrate to whom the arrangement applies and the Chief Magistrate.

The Governor in Council may appoint a Deputy Chief Magistrate, nominated by the Chief Magistrate, to be Acting Chief Magistrate during any period when the Chief Magistrate is absent on leave or for any reason is temporarily unable to perform the duties of the office of Chief Magistrate.

history.raw: S. 8(1AAA) inserted by No. 31/2013 s. 6(1).

nodes.text: The Governor in Council may appoint one of the magistrates (other than a reserve magistrate) to be Acting Chief Magistrate—

during any period when the Chief Magistrate is absent on leave or for any reason is temporarily unable to perform the duties of the office of Chief Magistrate if an appointment has not been made under subsection (1AAA); or
if there is a vacancy in the office of Chief Magistrate.
The senior of the Deputy Chief Magistrates willing to act as Chief Magistrate shall act as Chief Magistrate if there is—

history.raw: S. 8(1A) inserted by No. 64/1996 s. 28(1), substituted by No. 31/2013 s. 6(3).

nodes.text: a period when the Chief Magistrate is for any reason temporarily unable to perform the duties of the office of Chief Magistrate and an appointment has not been made under subsection (1AAA) or (1)(a); or
a vacancy in the office of Chief Magistrate and an appointment has not been made under subsection (1)(b).

If the appointment of 2 or more Deputy Chief Magistrates took place on the same date, the Deputy Chief Magistrates have seniority according to the seniority assigned in the instruments of appointment as Deputy Chief Magistrate, or if there is no such assignment, according to the order of their taking oath or affirmation of office.

history.raw: S. 8(1B) inserted by No. 64/1996 s. 28(1), amended by Nos 31/2013 s. 6(4), 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 81.1).

nodes.text: A magistrate who is appointed as Acting Chief Magistrate or acts as Chief Magistrate under subsection (1A) has, during the period of the appointment or the period of acting as Chief Magistrate, the same powers and duties as the Chief Magistrate.

history.raw: S. 9A inserted by No. 5/2013 s. 35.

nodes.text: The Governor in Council may appoint as many reserve magistrates as are necessary for transacting the business of the Court.
A person is not eligible for appointment as a reserve magistrate unless he or she—
has not attained the age of 78 years; and

history.raw: S. 9A(2)(a) amended by No. 63/2013 s. 41.

nodes.text: is, or has been—
a magistrate appointed under section 7 or any previous corresponding provision; or
a magistrate of a Magistrates' Court or Local Court (however designated) of another State or the Northern Territory or the Australian Capital Territory.
The instrument of appointment of a person as a reserve magistrate must specify the terms and conditions of appointment.
A reserve magistrate is eligible for re-appointment as a reserve magistrate.

history.raw: S. 9B inserted by No. 5/2013 s. 35.
S. 9B(2) repealed by No. 16/2016 s. 197.

nodes.text: A reserve magistrate ceases to hold office on the earlier of—
the end of 5 years from the date of his or her appointment as a reserve magistrate; or
attaining the age of 78 years.

history.raw: S. 9B(1)(b) amended by No. 63/2013 s. 42(1).

nodes.text: A reserve magistrate may resign by sending his or her resignation in writing to the Governor.

history.raw: S. 9B(1A) inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 42(2).

nodes.heading: Chief Magistrate may engage reserve magistrate to undertake duties of a magistrate

history.raw: S. 9C (Heading) amended by No. 63/2013 s. 43(1).
S. 9C inserted by No. 5/2013 s. 35.

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate may, from time to time, by notice in writing, engage a reserve magistrate to undertake the duties of a magistrate—

history.raw: S. 9C(1) amended by No. 63/2013 s. 43(2).

nodes.text: on a full time basis; or
on a sessional basis.
Without limiting subsection (1), an engagement under that subsection must specify the period of the engagement.
The Chief Magistrate does not have the power to revoke or amend a notice of engagement under subsection (1), other than with the consent of the reserve magistrate.

history.raw: S. 9C(3) amended by No. 63/2013 s. 43(3).

nodes.text: An engagement under subsection (1) must not exceed 6 months.

history.raw: S. 9C(4) inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 43(4).

nodes.text: For the purpose of deciding whether, when, or on what basis to engage a reserve magistrate to undertake duties, the Chief Magistrate may request the reserve magistrate to provide any information that the Chief Magistrate considers may be relevant to enable a decision to engage to be made.

history.raw: S. 9C(5) inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 43(4).

nodes.heading: Pension rights and service of Chief Magistrate not affected by being a reserve magistrate

history.raw: S. 9D inserted by No. 5/2013 s. 35.

nodes.text: Despite section 10A(2), appointment as a reserve magistrate does not affect the right of a person who was the Chief Magistrate before that appointment to a pension under section 10A.
Service as a reserve magistrate does not count as service in the office of Chief Magistrate for the purposes of section 10A.

nodes.heading: Powers, jurisdiction, immunities and protection of reserve magistrate
nodes.text: Subject to this Act, a reserve magistrate has the same powers, jurisdiction, immunities and protection as a magistrate when undertaking the duties of a magistrate in accordance with an engagement under section 9C.

history.raw: S. 9E inserted by No. 5/2013 s. 35.

nodes.heading: Power to complete matters—magistrates and reserve magistrates

history.raw: S. 9EA inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 44.

nodes.text: This section applies to—
a magistrate whose office ceases under section 12(a) or by resignation;
a reserve magistrate engaged under section 9C whose engagement expires;
a reserve magistrate engaged under section 9C—but only if at the time of that cessation or expiry the magistrate or reserve magistrate had a matter—
whose engagement expires; and
whose appointment as a reserve magistrate ceases, other than by way of resignation—
that was part-heard before him or her; or
in respect of which his or her decision or determination is pending.

Subject to subsection (4), a former magistrate, reserve magistrate or former reserve magistrate to whom this section applies may give judgment, make any order or complete or otherwise continue to deal with any matters relating to any proceeding that former magistrate, reserve magistrate or former reserve magistrate (as the case may be) had heard, or partly heard, before the cessation of his or her office or appointment or expiry of his or her engagement.
For the purposes of subsection (2)—
a reserve magistrate to whom this section applies whose engagement has expired is taken to be engaged under section 9C; and
a former magistrate or former reserve magistrate to whom this section applies—
holds office as a reserve magistrate by virtue of this section as if he or she had been appointed under section 9A; and
is taken to be a reserve magistrate engaged under section 9C; and

section 10(2) and Part 2 of Schedule 1 do not apply and that person is not entitled to remuneration and entitlements under that section for the period during which he or she is acting in accordance with subsection (2) after the cessation of his or her commission or appointment or the expiry of his or her engagement, as the case requires; and
the person may continue to serve as a reserve magistrate for the purposes of subsection (2) despite having attained the age of 78 years.
Subject to subsection (5), any appointment or engagement of a person under this section ceases on the earlier of—
the completion of the matters referred to in subsection (2); or
6 months from the date of that appointment or engagement; or
the person being appointed under section 9A as a reserve magistrate.
A person to whom this section applies may resign his or her office as reserve magistrate under this section by notice in writing to the Governor.
Nothing in this section prevents a person being appointed as a reserve magistrate under section 9A at any time, if he or she is eligible to be so appointed.
Nothing in this section affects the operation of section 16AB.
In this section a reference to "proceeding" includes—

history.raw: S. 9EA(8) inserted by No. 29/2015 s. 68.

nodes.text: any proceeding or other matter in the Children's Court under the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005; and
any investigation or inquiry under the Coroners Act 2008.

nodes.heading: Engaging in legal practice or other paid employment

history.raw: S. 9F inserted by No. 5/2013 s. 35, amended by No. 63/2013 s. 45 (ILA s. 39B(1)).

nodes.text: Except with the approval of the Chief Magistrate, a reserve magistrate must not engage in legal practice, undertake paid employment or conduct a business, trade or profession of any kind while engaged to undertake the duties of a magistrate under section 9C or acting under section 9EA.

Except with the approval of the Chief Magistrate, a reserve magistrate must not hold an office in any company, trustee company, incorporated association or other entity, whether public or private, in respect of which the reserve magistrate receives remuneration while engaged to undertake the duties of a magistrate under section 9C or acting under section 9EA.

history.raw: S. 9F(2) inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 45(2).

nodes.heading: Salaries, superannuation contributions, allowances and other conditions of service

history.raw: S. 10 (Heading) inserted by No. 29/2015 s. 84(1), substituted by No. 3/2016 s. 18(1).

nodes.text: Part 1 of Schedule 1 sets out—

history.raw: S. 10(1) amended by Nos 64/1990 s. 20(Sch. item 4.1), 29/2015 s. 84(2), substituted by No. 3/2016 s. 18(2).

nodes.text: the salaries payable to magistrates and the allowances and other conditions of service to which magistrates are entitled; and

history.raw: S. 10(1A)(a) amended by No. 1/2022 s. 16(2)(b).

nodes.text: the superannuation contributions payable for the benefit of magistrates.
The Chief Magistrate who is or has been a dual commission holder as a Judge of the Supreme Court—

history.raw: S. 10(1AA) inserted by No. 1/2022 s. 16(1).

nodes.text: is entitled to the salary and the allowances and other conditions of service of the Chief Magistrate who is or has been a dual commission holder as a Judge of the Supreme Court under this section and Schedule 1; and
is not entitled to receive any salary, allowances or other conditions of service as a Judge of the Supreme Court during the period of being a dual commission holder; and

in the case of the Chief Magistrate who has been a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court under the County Court Act 1958, is not entitled to receive any salary, allowances or other conditions of service as the Chief Magistrate who has been a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court.
The Chief Magistrate who has been a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court—

history.raw: S. 10(1A) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 34, amended by No. 1/2022 s. 16(2)(a).

nodes.text: is entitled to the salary and the allowances and other conditions of service of the Chief Magistrate who has been a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court under this section and Schedule 1; and
is not entitled to receive any salary, allowances or other conditions of service as a judge of the County Court under the County Court Act 1958 during the period of being a dual commission holder.
Part 2 of Schedule 1 sets out—

history.raw: S. 10(2) amended by Nos 64/1990 s. 20(Sch. item 4.1), 5/2013 s. 36, substituted by Nos 29/2015 s. 84(3), 3/2016 s. 18(3).

nodes.text: the salaries payable to reserve magistrates and the allowances and other conditions of service to which reserve magistrates are entitled; and
the superannuation contributions payable for the benefit of reserve magistrates.

history.raw: S. 10A inserted by No. 13/1999 s. 6.

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate and the partner and children of the Chief Magistrate are entitled to pensions in the same circumstances and at the same rates and on the same terms and conditions—

history.raw: S. 10A(1) amended by No. 23/2008 s. 20, substituted by No. 1/2022 s. 17(1).
Note to s. 10A(1) inserted by No. 29/2015 s. 69, repealed by No. 3/2016 s. 35(1).

nodes.text: in the case of the Chief Magistrate who is or has been a dual commission holder as a Judge of the Supreme Court—as a Judge of the Supreme Court and the partner and children of such a Judge are entitled to pensions under section 83 of the Constitution Act 1975; or

in the case of the Chief Magistrate who has been a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court but has not been a dual commission holder as a Judge of the Supreme Court—as a judge of the County Court (other than the Chief Judge) and the partner and children of such a judge are entitled to pensions under section 14 of the County Court Act 1958; or

in the case of the Chief Magistrate who has not been a dual commission holder—as a judge of the County Court (other than the Chief Judge) and the partner and children of such a judge are entitled to pensions under section 14 of the County Court Act 1958.

Subject to subsections (1AB) and (1C), section 83(6), (6B) and (6C) of the Constitution Act 1975 applies, with any necessary modification, in relation to the recognition of service for the purposes of a pension under this section if the Chief Magistrate is or has been a dual commission holder as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

history.raw: S. 10A(1AA) inserted by No. 1/2022 s. 17(2).

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate who is a dual commission holder as a Judge of the Supreme Court is taken to not hold the office of Judge of the Supreme Court during the period of being a dual commission holder as Judge of the Supreme Court when counting service in the office of Chief Magistrate.

history.raw: S. 10A(1AB) inserted by No. 1/2022 s. 17(2).

nodes.text: Subject to subsections (1B) and (1C), section 14(5) of the County Court Act 1958 applies, with any necessary modification, in relation to the recognition of service for the purposes of a pension under this section if the Chief Magistrate has been a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court or has not been a dual commission holder.

history.raw: S. 10A(1A) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 35(2), amended by No. 1/2022 s. 17(3).

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate who has been a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court is taken to not hold the office of judge of the County Court during the period of being a dual commission holder when counting service in the office of Chief Magistrate.

history.raw: S. 10A(1B) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 35(2), amended by No. 1/2022 s. 17(4).

nodes.text: If the Chief Magistrate—

history.raw: S. 10A(1C) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 35(2), substituted by No. 1/2022 s. 17(5).

nodes.text: is or has been a dual commission holder as a Judge of the Supreme Court, the person's service in the office of Chief Magistrate whilst a dual commission holder as a Judge of the Supreme Court, counts for the purposes of this section, as service in the office of Chief Magistrate; or

has been a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court, and is or has been a dual commission holder as a Judge of the Supreme Court, the person's service in the office of Chief Magistrate whilst a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court and as a Judge of the Supreme Court counts for the purposes of this section, as service in the office of Chief Magistrate; or

has been a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court, the person's service in the office of Chief Magistrate whilst a dual commission holder as a judge of the County Court counts for the purposes of this section, as service in the office of Chief Magistrate.
If the Chief Magistrate resigns the office of Chief Magistrate as a dual commission holder—

history.raw: S. 10A(1D) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 35(2), substituted by No. 1/2022 s. 17(6).

nodes.text: as a Judge of the Supreme Court but continues in the office of Judge of the Supreme Court, that person is taken not to have resigned or retired from the office of Chief Magistrate for the purposes of section 83(1), (1A), (1B), (1C) and (1D) of the Constitution Act 1975 as applied by this section; or

as a judge of the County Court but continues in the office of judge of the County Court, that person is taken not to have resigned or retired from the office of Chief Magistrate for the purposes of section 14(2), (2A) and (2B) of the County Court Act 1958 as applied by this section.
In the case of the death of a Chief Magistrate who is a dual commission holder, this section applies.

history.raw: S. 10A(1E) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 35(2).

nodes.text: A pension under this section is liable to be suspended or determined in the same circumstances and to the same extent as pensions under section 14 of the County Court Act 1958 or section 83 of the Constitution Act 1975, as the case requires, are liable to be suspended or determined.

history.raw: S. 10A(2) amended by No. 1/2022 s. 17(7).

nodes.text: A pension under this section may be commuted in the same circumstances and to the same extent as pensions under sections 14AC, 14AF and 14AI of the County Court Act 1958 or sections 83AA to 83AI of the Constitution Act 1975, as the case requires may be commuted and for that purpose sections 14AA to 14AI of the County Court Act 1958 or sections 83AA to 83AI of the Constitution Act 1975 apply with such modifications as are necessary.

history.raw: S. 10A(2A) inserted by No. 19/2001 s. 16(1), amended by No. 1/2022 s. 17(8).

nodes.text: Pensions under this section and any payments of lump sums provided by the commutation of those pensions are payable out of the Consolidated Fund which is hereby to the necessary extent appropriated accordingly.

history.raw: S. 10A(3) amended by No. 19/2001 s. 16(2).

nodes.text: This section applies in respect of the appointment of a Chief Magistrate made on or after 7 May 1996.
In this section—

history.raw: S. 10A(5) inserted by No. 4/2009 s. 37(Sch. 1 item 17).

nodes.heading: domestic partner
nodes.text: of a person means—

history.raw: S. 10A(5) def. of partner substituted by No. 40/2010 s. 109(1).

nodes.text: a person who is, or was at the time of the person's death, in a registered domestic relationship with the person; or

a person to whom the person is not married but with whom, in the opinion of the Minister, the person is, or was at the time of the person's death, living as a couple on a genuine domestic basis (irrespective of gender);

nodes.heading: partner
nodes.text: of a person means the person's spouse or domestic partner;

nodes.heading: spouse
nodes.text: of a person means a person to whom the person is, or was at the time of the person's death, married.
For the purposes of the definition of domestic

history.raw: S. 10A(6) inserted by No. 4/2009 s. 37(Sch. 1 item 17).

nodes.heading: partner
nodes.text: in subsection (5)—
registered domestic relationship has the same meaning as in the Relationships Act 2008; and

in determining whether persons who are not in a registered domestic relationship are domestic partners of each other, all the circumstances of their relationship are to be taken into account, including any one or more of the matters referred to in section 35(2) of the Relationships Act 2008 as may be relevant in a particular case.
