For the purposes of subsection (1), the definition of partner as substituted by section 109(1) of the Superannuation Legislation Amendment Act 2010 applies in respect of the entitlement to a pension of a partner of a Chief Magistrate or former Chief Magistrate only if the death of the Chief Magistrate or former Chief Magistrate occurs on or after the commencement of the substituting section.

history.raw: S. 10A(7) inserted by No. 40/2010 s. 109(2).

nodes.heading: Vacation of office
nodes.text: A person ceases to hold office as a magistrate if—

history.raw: S. 12 amended by No. 16/2005 s. 8(3)(a).

nodes.text: he or she attains the age of 70 years; or
he or she is removed from office by the Governor in Council in accordance with Part IIIAA of the Constitution Act 1975; or

history.raw: S. 12(b) substituted by No. 16/2005 s. 8(3)(c).

nodes.text: his or her office is abolished by or under an Act.

history.raw: S. 12(c) inserted by No. 16/2005 s. 8(3)(c).
S. 12A inserted by No. 16/2016 s. 198.

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate is responsible for ensuring the effective, orderly and expeditious discharge of the business of the Court.
The Chief Magistrate has the power to do all things necessary or convenient to be done to perform the Chief Magistrate's responsibilities under subsection (1).
Nothing in this section limits the responsibilities, functions or powers of the Chief Magistrate under this or any other Act.

history.raw: S. 13 amended by No. 64/1996 s. 29, substituted by No. 43/1998 s. 45.

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate may assign duties to a magistrate or judicial registrar.
A magistrate or judicial registrar must carry out the duties that are from time to time assigned to him or her by the Chief Magistrate.

nodes.heading: Delegation by the Chief Magistrate
nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate, by instrument, may delegate to any magistrate any of his or her powers under sections 6(1) and 13.

history.raw: S. 13A inserted by No. 43/1998 s. 45.
S. 13B inserted by No. 10/1999 s. 21, substituted by No. 24/2007 s. 5.

nodes.text: In this section—

nodes.heading: judicial officer
nodes.text: means—

history.raw: S. 13B(1) def. of judicial officer amended by No. 36/2007 s. 3(5).

nodes.text: a magistrate; or
a judicial registrar; or
the principal registrar, a registrar or a deputy registrar.
The Chief Magistrate is responsible for directing the professional development and continuing education and training of judicial officers.
In discharging his or her responsibility under subsection (2) the Chief Magistrate may direct—to participate in a specified professional development or continuing education and training activity.
all judicial officers; or
a specified class of judicial officer; or
a specified judicial officer—
A direction under subsection (3) may be given orally or in writing.

history.raw: S. 14 amended by No. 64/2010 s. 63 (ILA s. 39B(1)).

nodes.text: A magistrate has, in the performance of his or her duties as a magistrate, the same protection and immunity as a Judge of the Supreme Court has in the performance of his or her duties as a Judge.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the protection and immunity extends to the conduct of a committal proceeding.

history.raw: S. 14(2) inserted by No. 64/2010 s. 63.
Note to s. 15 inserted by No. 16/2016 s. 199.

nodes.text: A Council of the magistrates must meet at least once in each year on a day or days fixed by the Chief Magistrate to—
consider the operation of this Act and the Rules; and
consider the working of the offices of the Court and the arrangements relating to the duties of court officials; and
inquire into and examine any defects which appear to exist in the system of procedure or the administration of the law in the Court.
The Chief Magistrate must cause adequate notice of a meeting to be given to all the magistrates.
The magistrates must report annually to the Governor on the operation of the Court.
In this section, "magistrate" does not include a reserve magistrate.

history.raw: S. 15(4) inserted by No. 5/2013 s. 38(2).

nodes.text: A Chief Magistrate who is a dual commission holder is a member of the Council of magistrates and is also a member of the Council of Judges under section 28 of the Supreme Court Act 1986.

history.raw: S. 15(5) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 36, amended by No. 1/2022 s. 18.

nodes.text: See Divisions 1 and 2 of Part 6 of the Judicial Commission of Victoria Act 2016 which specifies functions for the Council of magistrates.

history.raw: S. 16 (Heading) inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 7(1).
S. 16(3) repealed by No. 64/1996 s. 30(2).
S. 16(4) repealed by No. 19/2005 s. 9(1).

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate together with one or more Deputy Chief Magistrates may jointly make rules of court for or with respect to the following—
any matter dealt with in the Rules referred to in subsection (5);

furthering the overarching purpose set out in the Civil Procedure Act 2010 and the conduct of civil proceedings in accordance with the principles set out in that Act, including the overarching obligations;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(ab) inserted by No. 47/2010 s. 89(a).

nodes.text: the conduct of civil proceedings and parties to civil proceedings generally, including, but not limited to, the imposition of limits, restrictions or conditions on any party in respect of any aspect of the conduct of civil proceedings;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(ac) inserted by No. 47/2010 s. 89(a).

nodes.text: case management;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(ad) inserted by No. 47/2010 s. 89(a).

nodes.text: discovery and disclosure;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(ada) inserted by No. 25/2014 s. 11.

nodes.text: any other matter or thing required or permitted by or under the Civil Procedure Act 2010 to be dealt with by rules of court or otherwise necessary or required for the purposes of that Act;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(ae) inserted by No. 47/2010 s. 89(a).

nodes.text: the prescription of the civil proceedings or class of civil proceedings which may be dealt with by the Court constituted by a registrar;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(b) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.17).

nodes.text: the prescription of any venue of the court as a civil registry court;
any other matter or thing required or permitted by or under the Open Courts Act 2013 to be dealt with by rules of court or otherwise necessary or required for the purposes of that Act;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(ca) inserted by No. 58/2013 s. 48.
S. 16(1A)(ca) inserted by No. 8/2008 s. 11, amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.18).

nodes.text: any matter or thing required or permitted by or under the Vexatious Proceedings Act 2014 to be dealt with by rules of court or otherwise necessary or required for the purposes of that Act;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(cb) inserted by No. 42/2014 s. 107.

nodes.text: any other matter or thing required or permitted by or under Part 4A of the Sex Offenders Registration Act 2004 to be dealt with by rules of court or otherwise necessary or required for the purposes of Part 4A of that Act;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(cc) inserted by No. 21/2016 s. 22.

nodes.text: the conduct of civil proceedings and parties to civil proceedings conducted in accordance with the Legal Identity of Defendants (Organisational Child Abuse) Act 2018, including, but not limited to—

history.raw: S. 16(1)(cd) inserted by No. 18/2018 s. 18.

nodes.text: the imposition of limits, restrictions or conditions on any party (including proper defendants) in respect of any aspect of the conduct of those proceedings; and

history.raw: S. 16(1)(i) inserted by No. 31/2001 s. 7(2).
S. 16(1A)(i) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.19).

nodes.text: the direction or ordering of parties (including proper defendants) to those proceedings; and

history.raw: S. 16(1)(h)(ii) amended by No. 31/2001 s. 7(1).

nodes.text: the modification of any rule, practice or procedure in its application to proper defendants under that Act; and
any other matter or thing necessary or required for the purposes of that Act or arising from civil proceedings conducted in accordance with that Act;

any matter or thing required or permitted by or under Division 5 of Part 5 of the Second-Hand Dealers and Pawnbrokers Act 1989 to be dealt with by rules of court or otherwise necessary or required for the purposes of Division 5 of Part 5 of that Act;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(ce) inserted by No. 3/2019 s. 30.

nodes.text: appeals in civil proceedings by way of re-hearing or otherwise to the Court constituted by a magistrate from the Court constituted by a registrar;
the payment of money into and out of court in civil proceedings and the investment of that money;
the service of documents in civil proceedings, including service outside Australia;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(ea) inserted by No. 10/1999 s. 22.

nodes.text: any matter relating to the practice and procedure of the Court in civil proceedings;
the reference of any civil proceeding or of any part of a civil proceeding to mediation;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(fa) inserted by No. 64/1996 s. 30(1)(b).

nodes.text: the referral of any civil proceeding, or any part of a civil proceeding, for a pre-hearing conference and the conduct of pre-hearing conferences;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(fb) inserted by No. 51/2000 s. 4.

nodes.text: judicial resolution conferences, including, but not limited to the practice and procedure of the Court in relation to judicial resolution conferences;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(fc) inserted by No. 50/2009 s. 14.

nodes.text: without limiting paragraphs (fa), (fb) and (fc), the referral, direction or ordering of parties to a civil proceeding to any form of appropriate dispute resolution, whether with or without the consent of the parties;

history.raw: S. 16(1)(fd) inserted by No. 47/2010 s. 89(b).

nodes.text: any matter relating to the enforcement of orders made by the Court in civil proceedings;
electronic communication and electronic processes, including, but not limited to—

history.raw: S. 16(1)(ga) inserted by No. 33/2018 s. 49(1).

nodes.text: applications by electronic means, electronic filing and electronic service of documents in any civil proceeding; and
the transmission and issuing of orders, processes and other documents by electronic communication; and
use of electronic signatures and seals;
the storage, disposal or destruction of documents—

history.raw: S. 16(1)(h) inserted by No. 33/1994 s. 5(1).

nodes.text: filed or lodged with the appropriate registrar in civil proceedings; or
issued out of the Court in civil proceedings and kept by the principal registrar;

the conduct of, and procedure for, or in relation to, substituted proceedings to which Part 3A of the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 1998 applies including, but not limited to, the form or manner in which substituted proceedings are to be commenced.
The Chief Magistrate together with one or more Deputy Chief Magistrates may jointly make rules of court for or with respect to the following—

history.raw: S. 16(1A) inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 7(2), amended by No. 20/2022 s. 34(1).
S. 16(1A)(m) amended by No. 12/2006 s. 169(c), repealed by No. 47/2014 s. 269.

nodes.text: prescribing by scale or otherwise the costs of and incidental to criminal proceedings in the Court;
prescribing a method for the electronic filing of charge-sheets;
electronic communication and electronic processes, including, but not limited to—

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(ba) inserted by No. 33/2018 s. 49(2).

nodes.text: applications by electronic means, electronic filing and electronic service of documents in any criminal proceeding; and
the transmission and issuing of orders, processes and other documents by electronic communication; and
use of electronic signatures and seals;
the form in which process may be issued out of the Court and the manner in which it may be authenticated, stored, transmitted or otherwise dealt with;
any matter relating to sentence indications under Division 3 of Part 3.3 of Chapter 3 of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009;
the manner in which orders may be authenticated;
any matter relating to the practice and procedure of the Koori Court Division of the Court;
the transfer of proceedings to and from the Koori Court Division of the Court;
any matter relating to the practice and procedure of the Specialist Family Violence Court Division of the Court;
the transfer of proceedings to and from the Specialist Family Violence Court Division of the Court;

the causes of action or claims, or classes of causes of action or claims, or proceedings or classes of proceedings, that may be heard and determined in the Neighbourhood Justice Division of the Court;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(ha) inserted by No. 51/2006 s. 5.

nodes.text: any matter relating to the practice and procedure of the Neighbourhood Justice Division of the Court;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(hb) inserted by No. 51/2006 s. 5.

nodes.text: the transfer of proceedings to and from the Neighbourhood Justice Division of the Court;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(hc) inserted by No. 51/2006 s. 5.

nodes.text: any matter relating to the practice and procedure of the Assessment and Referral Court List;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(hd) inserted by No. 12/2010 s. 6.

nodes.text: the transfer of proceedings to and from the Assessment and Referral Court List;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(he) inserted by No. 12/2010 s. 6.

nodes.text: the procedure to be followed on a proceeding held under an order made under Part 4.3 of Chapter 4 of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009;
any matter relating to the practice and procedure of the Court in committal proceedings;
the return to the Court of warrants issued under section 57;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(k) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.20), new s. 16(1A)(k) inserted by No. 38/2017 s. 70.

nodes.text: forms to be used in committal proceedings;
prescribing persons or classes of persons for the purposes of item 30 of Schedule 3 to the Criminal Procedure Act 2009;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(la) inserted by No. 38/2008 s. 8, amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.21).

nodes.text: prescribing the rules, practice and procedure applicable to the execution of a warrant to seize property issued for the enforcement of an order made by the Court in a criminal proceeding;
the storage, disposal or destruction of documents—
filed or lodged with the appropriate registrar in criminal proceedings; or
issued out of the Court in criminal proceedings and kept by the principal registrar;
requirements for the purposes of Part IIA of the Evidence (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1958 for or with respect to—

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(p) amended by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 2 item 32).

nodes.text: the form of audio visual or audio link;
the equipment, or class of equipment, used to establish the link;
the layout of cameras;
the standard, or speed, of transmission;
the quality of communication;
any other matter relating to the link;
applications to the Court under Division 2 or 3 of Part IIA of the Evidence (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1958;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(q) amended by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 2 item 32).

nodes.text: any matter relating to the practice and procedure of the Court under Part IIA of the Evidence (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1958;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(r) amended by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 2 item 32).

nodes.text: the forms to be used in criminal proceedings;
the matters to be considered in determining the last known place of residence or business of a person for the purpose of service of a document on the person in a criminal proceeding;

history.raw: S. 16(1A)(t) substituted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.22).

nodes.text: the recording of proceedings in the Court;
generally, any matter relating to the practice and procedure of the Court in criminal proceedings.
Rules made under subsection (1A) must not be inconsistent with the Criminal Procedure Act 2009.

history.raw: S. 16(1AB) inserted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.23).

nodes.text: Without limiting any other power to make rules of court conferred by this or any other Act, the Chief Magistrate together with one or more Deputy Chief Magistrates may jointly make rules of court for or with respect to generally prescribing any matter or thing required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed by rules of court or necessary to be prescribed by rules of court to give effect to this Act.

history.raw: S. 16(1B) inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 7(2), amended by No. 20/2022 s. 34(1).

nodes.text: In exercising a power conferred by subsection (1A)(j), (k) or (l) to make rules, the Chief Magistrate and the Deputy Chief Magistrate or Magistrates, as the case requires, must have regard to the interests of the community in ensuring the prompt and efficient disposal of criminal proceedings.

history.raw: S. 16(1C) inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 7(2), amended by No. 20/2022 s. 34(2).

nodes.text: A power conferred by this Act to make rules may be exercised—

history.raw: S. 16(1D) inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 7(2).

nodes.text: either in relation to all cases to which the power extends, or in relation to all those cases subject to specified exceptions, or in relation to any specified case or class of case; and
so as to make, as respects the cases in relation to which it is exercised—

the same provision for all cases in relation to which the power is exercised, or different provisions for different cases or classes of case, or different provisions for the same case or class of case for different purposes; or
any such provision either unconditionally or subject to any specified condition.
Rules made under this Act may be made so as to—

history.raw: S. 16(1E) inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 7(2).

nodes.text: require a matter affected by the rules to be approved by or to the satisfaction of a specified court official or a specified class of court official; and
confer a discretionary authority or impose a duty on a specified person or a specified class of person; and

provide in a specified case or class of case for the exemption of proceedings or a class of proceeding from any of the provisions of the rules, whether unconditionally or on specified conditions and either wholly or to such an extent as is specified.

The power of the Chief Magistrate together with one or more Deputy Chief Magistrates to jointly make rules of court, whether that power is conferred by this or any other Act, is subject to the rules being disallowed by a House of the Parliament in accordance with section 23 of the Subordinate Legislation Act 1994.

history.raw: S. 16(2) substituted by No. 64/1996 s. 30(2), amended by No. 20/2022 s. 34(1).

nodes.text: The proposed Magistrates' Court Civil Procedure Rules 1989 approved by a majority of the magistrates on 17 March 1989—as if they had been made under this Act on the day on which this Act received the Royal Assent.
are for all purposes (including the purposes of the Subordinate Legislation Act 1962) to be treated; and
have effect; and
may be revoked or amended—

history.raw: S. 16A inserted by No. 64/1996 s. 31.

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate may from time to time issue practice directions, statements or notes for the Court in relation to civil or criminal proceedings or any class of civil or criminal proceedings.
Practice directions, statements or notes issued under subsection (1) must not be inconsistent with any provision made by or under this or any other Act.

nodes.heading: Constitution of Court if magistrate unable to continue and constitution of Court in certain circumstances

history.raw: S. 16AB inserted by No. 63/2013 s. 46.

nodes.text: Subject to subsection (2), despite anything in any Act or the rules, any power, duty or act which might have been exercised or performed by the Court constituted by a magistrate may be exercised or performed by the Court constituted by any other magistrate if the Court cannot for any reason be constituted by that first mentioned magistrate.

If this Act or the rules provide that a division of the Court must be constituted by a magistrate assigned to that division, the Court may only be constituted under subsection (1) by a magistrate who is assigned to the relevant division.

For the avoidance of doubt, for the purpose of completion of any matter whether under section 9EA or otherwise, the Court may be constituted or continue to be constituted by a reserve magistrate who is a magistrate without reconstitution of the Court despite any interruption in continuity of his or her tenure, appointment or engagement.

history.raw: Pt 2A (Heading and ss 16B–16K) inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.heading: Guidelines relating to the appointment of judicial registrars

history.raw: S. 16B inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate may, in consultation with the Attorney-General—
prepare guidelines relating to the appointment (including re-appointment) of judicial registrars of the Court; and

history.raw: S. 16B(1)(a) amended by No. 62/2014 s. 90.

nodes.text: from time to time amend or revoke any guidelines prepared under paragraph (a).

The Chief Magistrate must, as soon as practicable after preparing, amending or revoking any guidelines under subsection (1), cause a copy of the guidelines or the amendment or notice of the revocation (as the case requires) to be given to the Attorney-General.

history.raw: S. 16C inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate may, at any time, having regard to any guidelines in force under section 16B(1), recommend to the Attorney-General that a judicial registrar, or more than one judicial registrar, of the Court be appointed by the Governor in Council.

The Attorney-General, on receiving a recommendation under subsection (1), may recommend to the Governor in Council that a judicial registrar, or more than one judicial registrar, of the Court be appointed under subsection (3).

history.raw: S. 16C(2) amended by No. 34/2010 s. 50.

nodes.text: The Governor in Council, on the recommendation of the Attorney-General, may appoint a person as a judicial registrar of the Court for the period, not exceeding 5 years, specified in his or her instrument of appointment.
A person is not eligible for appointment as a judicial registrar unless he or she is—
an Australian lawyer; or

history.raw: S. 16C(4)(a) substituted by No. 19/2005 s. 6, amended by No. 17/2014 s. 160(Sch. 2 item 59.3).

nodes.text: enrolled as a legal practitioner of the High Court of Australia.
A judicial registrar may be appointed on a full-time or part-time basis.

A judicial registrar, although not appointed on a part-time basis, may, by agreement in writing entered into with the Chief Magistrate, undertake the duties of a judicial registrar on a part-time basis.
A judicial registrar is eligible for re-appointment in accordance with this section if the Chief Magistrate recommends to the Attorney-General that the person be re-appointed.

history.raw: S. 16C(7) amended by No. 62/2014 s. 91.

nodes.text: The Public Administration Act 2004 does not apply to a judicial registrar in respect of the office of judicial registrar.

history.raw: S. 16D inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.text: A judicial registrar is entitled to the terms and conditions including remuneration and allowances that are fixed in respect of him or her from time to time by the Governor in Council.

history.raw: S. 16D(1) amended by No. 29/2015 s. 70(1).

nodes.text: Except with the approval of the Attorney-General, a judicial registrar must not engage in legal practice, undertake paid employment or conduct a business, trade or profession of any kind.

A judicial registrar must disclose to the Chief Magistrate in writing any direct or indirect pecuniary interest that he or she has or acquires that could conflict with the proper performance of the duties of the office of judicial registrar.

Despite any provision to the contrary made by or under any other Act, a person who has held the office of judicial registrar is entitled to have his or her service in that office taken into account in computing the period of service which entitles public officials (within the meaning of the Public Administration Act 2004) to be granted long service leave or other leave entitlements, whether his or her service in the office of judicial registrar is before or after any period of service as such a public official.
The following are to be paid out of the Consolidated Fund, which is appropriated to the necessary extent—

history.raw: S. 16D(5) inserted by No. 29/2015 s. 70(2).

nodes.text: the amounts (including the amount of any non-salary benefits) payable to or for any judicial registrar; and
premiums and other amounts payable under the Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2013 in respect of any judicial registrar; and
payroll tax payable under the Payroll Tax Act 2007 in respect of wages paid or payable to any judicial registrar; and
tax payable under the Fringe Benefits Tax Act 1986 of the Commonwealth in respect of fringe benefits provided to any judicial registrar; and
superannuation contributions within the meaning of the Payroll Tax Act 2007 payable in respect of any judicial registrar.
In this section, non-salary benefits has the same meaning as it has in clause 3(5) and (6) of Schedule 1A to the Public Administration Act 2004.

history.raw: S. 16D(6) inserted by No. 29/2015 s. 70(2).

nodes.text: Nothing in this section authorises the salary or the aggregate value of the allowances payable to a judicial registrar to be reduced.

history.raw: S. 16D(7) inserted by No. 62/2014 s. 92.
S. 16DB inserted by No. 62/2014 s. 93.

nodes.text: A judicial registrar must take an oath or affirmation of office in the prescribed form and manner.

Subsection (1) only applies to a person who is appointed or re-appointed as a judicial registrar on or after the commencement of section 93 of the Courts Legislation Miscellaneous Amendments Act 2014.
A failure by a person to take an oath or affirmation of office in accordance with this section does not invalidate anything done by that person as a judicial registrar.

nodes.heading: Resignation from office
nodes.text: A judicial registrar may resign from office by delivering to the Governor a signed letter of resignation.

history.raw: S. 16E inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.heading: Rules of Court
nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate together with one or more Deputy Chief Magistrates may jointly make rules of court for or with respect to—

history.raw: S. 16I inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5, amended by No. 20/2022 s. 35.

nodes.text: the prescription of the proceedings or class of proceedings which may be dealt with by the Court constituted by a judicial registrar;
delegating to the judicial registrars all or any of the powers of the Court except the power—

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(ii) repealed by No. 65/2011 s. 107(Sch. item 8.1).

nodes.text: to impose a sentence of imprisonment or of detention in a youth justice centre or youth residential centre; or

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(i) amended by No. 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 22.2).

nodes.text: to make a drug and alcohol treatment order within the meaning of the Sentencing Act 1991; or

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(iii) amended by No. 43/2020 s. 38.

nodes.text: to make a Court Secure Treatment Order within the meaning of the Sentencing Act 1991; or

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(iv) amended by No. 69/2005 s. 28, substituted by No. 26//2014 s. 455(Sch. item 20.2).

nodes.text: to hear and determine an appeal made to the Court; or

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(v) amended by No. 65/2011 s. 107(Sch. item 8.2).

nodes.text: to make a community correction order within the meaning of the Sentencing Act 1991;

history.raw: S. 16I(b)(vi) inserted by No. 65/2011 s. 107(Sch. item 8.3), amended by No. 62/2014 s. 94(a).

nodes.text: reviews of, and appeals from, the court constituted by a judicial registrar.

history.raw: S. 16I(c) inserted by No. 62/2014 s. 94(b).

nodes.heading: Performance of duties by judicial registrar

history.raw: S. 16J inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5.

nodes.text: A judicial registrar must not hear, or continue to hear, a proceeding that the judicial registrar considers for any reason inappropriate for hearing and determination by the Court constituted by a judicial registrar and must make appropriate arrangements for the proceeding to be heard and determined by the Court constituted by a magistrate.
A judicial registrar, in the performance of his or her duties as a judicial registrar, is not subject to the direction or control of any person or body.

A judicial registrar has, in the performance of his or her duties as a judicial registrar, the same protection and immunity as a Judge of the Supreme Court has in the performance of his or her duties as a Judge.
A judicial registrar has any of the powers, duties and functions of a registrar under this Act and any other Act or the Rules.

history.raw: S. 16J(4) inserted by No. 17/2023 s. 36.

nodes.heading: Appeal from or review of determination of Court constituted by judicial registrar

history.raw: S. 16K inserted by No. 19/2005 s. 5, substituted by No. 62/2014 s. 95.

nodes.text: The rules may provide for appeals from or reviews of a determination of the Court constituted by a judicial registrar—
whether in respect of—
the hearing and determination of any proceeding (whether criminal or civil); or
any interlocutory application; and
whether in respect of specified kinds of application or proceeding or generally; and
by specifying whether the procedure is by way of appeal or review or both; and
by specifying the way in which the Court may be constituted for those appeals or reviews.
The powers in subsection (1) are in addition to and do not limit any power to make rules under section 16I.
Unless the rules otherwise provide, a determination of the Court constituted by a judicial registrar may be appealed from or reviewed—
on application of a party to the proceeding; or
on the Court's own motion.
If the rules do not provide for an appeal from or a review of a determination of the Court constituted by a judicial registrar, the determination is to be subject to a review or an appeal conducted—
by way of hearing de novo by the Court constituted by a magistrate; and
otherwise in accordance with the rules, if any.

nodes.heading: Employment of principal registrar, registrars and deputy registrars

history.raw: S. 17(1A)(1B) inserted by No. 10/1999 s. 23, amended by No. 108/2004 s. 117(1) (Sch. 3 item 118.2), repealed by No. 1/2014 s. 72.

nodes.text: For the purposes of this Act and to assist in the administration of the Court there are to be employed under Part 3 of the Public Administration Act 2004—
a principal registrar; and
as many registrars and deputy registrars as are necessary.
The principal registrar, registrars and deputy registrars have the duties, powers and functions provided by this Act and the Fines Reform Act 2014, the regulations and the Rules.

The principal registrar may, by instrument, delegate to any registrar or class of registrars any function or power of the principal registrar under this Act and the Fines Reform Act 2014, the regulations or the Rules, except this power of delegation.
A deputy registrar may, subject to this Act, the regulations and the Rules and to any directions of a registrar, exercise any of the powers or perform any of the functions of a registrar.

nodes.heading: Appointment of Aboriginal elders or respected persons

history.raw: S. 17A inserted by No. 27/2002 s. 7.

nodes.text: The Chief Executive Officer may appoint a person who is a member of the Aboriginal community as an Aboriginal elder or respected person for the purpose of performing functions in relation to the Koori Court Division of the Court as set out in this Act.

history.raw: S. 17A(1) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 3(1).

nodes.text: An Aboriginal elder or respected person holds office for the period, and on the terms and conditions, determined by the Chief Executive Officer and specified in the instrument of appointment.

history.raw: S. 17A(2) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 3(1).

nodes.text: An Aboriginal elder or respected person may resign from office by writing signed by him or her and delivered to the Chief Executive Officer.

history.raw: S. 17A(3) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 3(1).

nodes.text: In this section—

history.raw: S. 17A(4) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 3(2).

nodes.heading: Chief Executive Officer
nodes.text: means the Chief Executive Officer of Court Services Victoria appointed under section 22 of the Court Services Victoria Act 2014.
The principal registrar must cause a register to be kept of all the orders of the Court and of such other matters as are directed by this Act or the Rules to be entered in the register.
An order made by the Court must be authenticated by the person who constituted the Court.
Any person may, subject to any order made under Part 3 of the Open Courts Act 2013 and on payment of the prescribed fee, inspect that part of the register that contains the final orders of the Court.

history.raw: S. 18(3) amended by No. 58/2013 s. 49.

nodes.text: A party to a proceeding may inspect without charge that part of the register that relates to that proceeding.

A document purporting to be an extract from the register and purporting to be signed by a registrar who certifies that in his or her opinion the extract is a true extract from the register is admissible in evidence in any proceedings and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, is proof of the matters appearing in the extract.

nodes.heading: Offence to publish certain information concerning proceedings
nodes.text: A person must not, in the course of a business of publishing information concerning debtors, publish or cause to be published any information concerning the commencement of a proceeding for debt so as to identify the defendant before a final order is made in the proceeding. Penalty: 100 penalty units.

nodes.heading: Recording of proceedings
nodes.text: The principal registrar must ensure that all proceedings in the Court are recorded in accordance with the Rules.

history.raw: S. 19A inserted by No. 51/2000 s. 5.

nodes.text: Process may only be issued out of the Court by a registrar, except where otherwise provided by or under this or any other Act.
The principal registrar must, subject to the regulations, keep the original of all process issued out of the Court and must issue or cause to be issued as many copies as are necessary.
Process issued by a registrar may be recalled and cancelled by—
that registrar; or
if that registrar is dead or has ceased to hold office or cannot be located, a magistrate.
A registrar has the following powers in addition to those conferred on him or her by this or any other Act or the Rules—
power to issue any process out of the Court;
power to administer an oath or affirmation;

history.raw: S. 21(1)(b) amended by No. 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 81.1).

nodes.text: power to abridge or extend the bail of a person who has been granted bail in relation to a criminal proceeding;
power to endorse a warrant to arrest in accordance with section 62;
power to sign any licence or certificate which the Court is authorised to issue;
power to hear and determine any application, and exercise any power or authority of the Court, under section 58, 59 or 60 of the Supreme Court Act 1986;
power to make a declaration under Division 4 of Part 7 of the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016;

history.raw: S. 21(1)(g) inserted by No. 53/2016 s. 109(b), amended by No. 11/2021 s. 54(1)(b).

nodes.text: power to adjourn a criminal proceeding or a proceeding under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008, the Personal Safety Intervention Orders Act 2010 or the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016;

power to abridge or extend the adjournment of a criminal proceeding or a proceeding under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008, the Personal Safety Intervention Orders Act 2010 or the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016;

power to otherwise change the time or place at which a criminal proceeding or a proceeding under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008, the Personal Safety Intervention Orders Act 2010 or the National Domestic Violence Order Scheme Act 2016 is listed before the Court.
Nothing in this section empowers a registrar to vary the amount or conditions of bail.
The power under subsection (1)(c) to abridge or extend the bail of a person may be exercised—

history.raw: S. 21(3) inserted by No. 11/2021 s. 54(3).

nodes.text: at any time, including on the day on which the person's proceeding is listed before the Court; and
either in the presence or absence of the person.
The powers under subsection (1)(h), (i) and (j) in respect of a proceeding may be exercised—

history.raw: S. 21(4) inserted by No. 11/2021 s. 54(3).

nodes.text: at any time, including on the day on which the proceeding is listed before the Court; and
either in the presence or absence of the parties.
The powers under subsection (1)(c), (h), (i) and (j) may be exercised—

history.raw: S. 21(5) inserted by No. 11/2021 s. 54(3).

nodes.text: on the application of a party; or
on the registrar's own initiative.

history.raw: S. 22 amended by No. 9/1995 s. 11(3)(a).

nodes.text: Subject to subsection (2), a registrar must demand and receive the prescribed fees.

Subject to the regulations or any power to waive, postpone, remit or refund a prescribed fee in a civil proceeding, the appropriate registrar may, having regard to the income, day to day living expenses, liabilities and assets of the person liable to pay the fee, waive payment of that fee if, in his or her opinion, the payment of that fee by that person would cause him or her financial hardship and, in that case, that prescribed fee is not payable.

history.raw: S. 22(2) inserted by No. 9/1995 s. 11(3)(b), amended by No. 15/2018 s. 47.

nodes.text: Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply to fees payable to the sheriff.

history.raw: S. 22(3) inserted by No. 64/1996 s. 32.

nodes.heading: Extortion by and impersonation of court officials
nodes.text: The following persons are guilty of an offence and liable to a fine of not more than 20 penalty units or to imprisonment for a term of not more than 2 years or to both—
a court official who extorts, demands, takes or accepts from any person any unauthorised fee or reward;
a court official who pretends to be the holder of an office or position in or in relation to the Court which he or she does not hold;
any person who is not a court official and who pretends to be a court official.

nodes.heading: Protection of registrars
nodes.text: The principal registrar, a registrar and a deputy registrar have, in the performance of their duties in good faith, the same protection and immunity as a magistrate has in the performance of his or her duties as a magistrate.

history.raw: S. 24 amended by No. 64/2010 s. 64.

nodes.text: The Court has jurisdiction—
to hear and determine all summary offences; and
to hear and determine all indictable offences which may be heard and determined summarily; and
to conduct committal proceedings into indictable offences and either—
direct the accused to be tried and order that the accused be remanded in custody until trial or grant bail; or

history.raw: S. 25(1)(c)(i) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.25).

nodes.text: discharge the accused under section 126(4) of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009; and
to make orders to enforce the payment of all fines which are, by any Act, directed to be recovered in the Court or for the recovery of which no provision is made.
The jurisdiction given by subsection (1) is additional to any other jurisdiction given to the Court with respect to a criminal proceeding by or under any Act other than this Act.
In a particular case, the jurisdiction given by subsection (1)(c) may be exercised concurrently with the jurisdiction of the Children's Court to conduct a committal proceeding if—

history.raw: S. 25(3) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 ss 46(a), 54(l)).

nodes.text: the charges against each accused could properly be joined in the same indictment; and
the accused who is a child—
is of or over the age of 15 years at the time the proceeding against the child for the offence is commenced; and

is charged with murder, attempted murder, manslaughter, child homicide, homicide by firearm, a designated offence (within the meaning of section 516 of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005) committed when the child was aged 15 years or over, an offence against section 197A of the Crimes Act 1958 (arson causing death) or an offence against section 318 of the Crimes Act 1958 (culpable driving causing death); and

the Court makes an order under subsection (4) in relation to the accused who is not a child and the Children's Court makes an order under section 516A(2) of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005 in relation to the accused who is a child.
The Court may order that joint committal proceedings in relation to a particular accused are appropriate having regard to—

history.raw: S. 25(4) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 ss 46(b), 54(l)).

nodes.text: the age of the child; and
the effect on victims of the offence charged if the committal proceedings were not conducted jointly; and
the estimated duration of the committal proceedings if conducted jointly; and
the number of witnesses that would be cross-examined by both accused; and
any other matter considered relevant.
The Court may make an order under subsection (4) on the application of a party or on its own motion.

history.raw: S. 25(5) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(l)).

nodes.text: Each party is entitled to be present and may address the Court when the Court is considering the making of an order under subsection (4).

history.raw: S. 25(6) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(l)).

nodes.text: If the Court makes an order under subsection (4), the Court may adjourn the proceeding for a period not exceeding 28 days to enable the Children's Court to determine whether joint committal proceedings are appropriate in the particular case.

history.raw: S. 25(7) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(l)).

nodes.text: If joint committal proceedings are conducted under subsection (3)—with any necessary modifications to ensure that the joint committal proceedings are conducted fairly and efficiently.

history.raw: S. 25(8) inserted by No. 7/2009 s. 426 (as amended by No. 68/2009 ss 46(c), 54(l)).

nodes.text: the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005 applies as far as practicable to the child; and
the Criminal Procedure Act 2009 applies as far as practicable to the other accused—

history.raw: Pt 4 Div. 2 (Heading) repealed by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(c) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).
Pt 4 Div. 2 Subdiv. 1 (Heading) repealed by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(c) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).
Pt 4 Div. 2 (Heading) inserted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.26).
Pt 4 Div. 2 Subdiv. 2 (Heading) repealed by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(c) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).

Pt 4 Div. 2 Subdiv. 4 (Heading and s. 56) amended by Nos 64/1990 s. 20(Sch. item 4.2), 43/1994 s. 56(Sch. item 3.1), 10/1999 ss 5, 8(2)(3), 92/2000 ss 5, 6, 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 22.4), 50/2006 ss 24, 25, repealed by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(c) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).

nodes.heading: Magistrate may exercise registrar's powers
nodes.text: A magistrate may exercise any of the powers of a registrar for the purpose of issuing criminal process.
The Court or a registrar may issue the following witness summonses—
summons to give evidence;

history.raw: S. 43(9)(a) repealed by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.3).

nodes.text: summons to produce documents or things;
summons to give evidence and produce documents or things.
Any party to a criminal proceeding in the Court may apply for the issue of a witness summons.
A witness summons may be directed to any person who appears to the Court or registrar issuing the summons to be likely—
to be able to give material evidence for any party to the proceeding; or
to have in the person's possession or control any documents or things which may be relevant on the hearing of the proceeding; or
both to be able to give material evidence and to have in the person's possession or control any relevant documents or things.
A witness summons must require the person to whom it is directed to attend at a specified venue of the Court on a certain date and at a certain time—
to give evidence in the proceeding; or
to produce for examination at the hearing any documents or things described in the summons that are in the person's possession or control; or
both to give evidence and produce for examination any documents or things described in the summons that are in the person's possession or control.
A witness summons must be served a reasonable time before the day on which the proceeding is listed before the Court.

history.raw: S. 43(5) substituted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.27).

nodes.text: A witness summons must be served by—

history.raw: S. 43(5A) inserted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.27).

nodes.text: giving a copy of the summons to the person to be served; or
if the person does not accept the copy, putting the copy down in the person's presence and telling the person the nature of the summons; or
leaving a copy of the summons for the person at the person's last known or usual place of residence or business with a person who appears to be of or over the age of 16 years.

If the person to be served is a company or registered body (within the meaning of the Corporations Act), a witness summons may be served on the company or body in accordance with section 109X or 601CX of that Act, as the case requires.

history.raw: S. 43(5B) inserted by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.27).

nodes.text: A person to whom a witness summons is directed is, subject to subsection (7), excused from complying with the summons unless conduct money is given or tendered to the person at the time of service of the summons or a reasonable time before the return date.
It is not necessary to give or tender conduct money to a person to whom a witness summons is directed if the person will not reasonably incur any expenses in complying with the summons.

The Court may direct that a witness who has attended before the Court in answer to a witness summons is entitled to receive from the party who applied for the issue of the witness summons further conduct money for each day of attendance.
Nothing in this section—
derogates from the power of the Court to certify that a witness be paid his or her expenses of attending before the Court.

Unless the Court or the registrar issuing the summons otherwise directs, a summons to produce documents or things or a summons to give evidence and produce documents or things permits the person to whom the summons is directed, instead of producing the document or thing at the hearing, to produce it, together with a copy of the summons, to the appropriate registrar not later than 2 days before the first day on which production is required.
If a document or thing is produced to the appropriate registrar under subsection (1), he or she must—
if requested to do so, give a receipt to the person producing the document or thing; and
produce the document or thing as the Court directs.

The production of a document or thing to the appropriate registrar under subsection (1) in answer to a summons to give evidence and produce documents or things does not remove the requirement on the person to whom the summons is directed to attend for the purpose of giving evidence.

history.raw: S. 45 amended by No. 11/2021 s. 55 (ILA s. 39B(1)).

nodes.text: A person whose attendance before the Court in a criminal proceeding has been required by witness summons must—until excused by the Court.
subject to section 43(6), attend at the time and place specified in the summons; and
if the proceeding is adjourned, attend at the time and place to which the proceeding has been adjourned, without the issue of a further summons—

A witness is not required to attend court on the date and time specified in a witness summons under subsection (1)(a), if the criminal proceeding is adjourned prior to the date and time specified in that summons.

history.raw: S. 45(2) inserted by No. 11/2021 s. 55.

nodes.heading: Power to amend where there is a defect or error

nodes.text: On the hearing of a proceeding the Court must not allow an objection to a warrant on account of any defect or error in it in substance or in form or for any variance between it and the evidence presented in the proceeding but the Court may amend the warrant to correct the defect or error.

history.raw: S. 50(1) amended by No. 7/2009 s. 427(1)(e) (as amended by No. 68/2009 s. 54(m)).

nodes.text: An order must not be set aside or quashed only because of a defect or error in form but the Court may amend the order to correct the defect or error.

history.raw: Pt 4 Div. 3 Subdiv. 7 (Heading and ss 82A–82F) inserted by No. 33/1994 s. 11(1), amended by Nos 45/1996 s. 18(Sch. 2 item 9.4), 70/1996 s. 7, 84/1997 s. 52, 99/2000 s. 3, 3/2005 s. 26, repealed by No. 12/2006 s. 176(1).
Pt 4 Div. 3 Subdiv. 8 (Heading and ss 82G–82I) inserted by No. 99/2000 s. 4.
S. 57(10) repealed by No. 38/2017 s. 71.

nodes.text: The following warrants may be issued—
warrant to arrest;
remand warrant;
search warrant;
warrant to seize property;
warrant to imprison;
warrant to detain in a youth justice centre;

history.raw: S. 57(1)(f) amended by No. 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 22.4).

nodes.text: enforcement warrant.

history.raw: S. 57(1)(g) inserted by No. 33/1994 s. 9(1), substituted by No. 32/2006 s. 88(2), amended by No. 47/2014 s. 271.

nodes.text: A warrant may be issued in paper form or electronically in accordance with this Division.

history.raw: S. 57(1AA) inserted by No. 33/2018 s. 50(1).

nodes.text: A warrant may be issued electronically by the person issuing the warrant causing the warrant, or the prescribed particulars of the warrant, to be transmitted electronically to the person to whom the warrant is issued in accordance with the regulations, if any.

history.raw: S. 57(1A) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 4(1), substituted by No. 33/2018 s. 50(2).

nodes.text: A warrant issued in accordance with subsection (1A)—

history.raw: S. 57(1B) inserted by No. 3/2016 s. 4(1).

nodes.text: directs and authorises the person to whom it is issued to do all things that the person would have been directed or authorised to do if a warrant containing the particulars referred to in subsection (1A) had been issued in paper form under subsection (1) by the person issuing the warrant; and
must not be amended, altered or varied after its issue, unless the amendment, alteration or variation is authorised by or under this Act or any other Act.
The person issuing a warrant must cause the prescribed particulars of the warrant to be entered in the register.
A warrant must name or otherwise describe the person or property against whom or which it is issued.
All warrants, other than a search warrant, may be issued by a registrar, a judicial registrar or a magistrate.
A search warrant may only be issued by a magistrate.
Remand warrants may be issued by a bail justice.

A judge of the Supreme Court or judge of the County Court may exercise any power conferred on a magistrate by or under this Act with respect to the issue, recall or cancellation of a warrant or duplicate copy of a warrant.

The registrar of the County Court, the Prothonotary of the Supreme Court or the Registrar of Criminal Appeals, as the case requires, may issue a warrant to imprison in the circumstances set out in sections 263(4), 266(3A) and 267(1A) of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009.

The registrar of the County Court, the Prothonotary of the Supreme Court or the Registrar of Criminal Appeals, as the case requires, may issue a warrant to detain in a youth justice centre or a youth residential centre in the circumstances set out in sections 430(4), 430C(5) and 430D(1A) of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005.

A warrant must be executed by the use of a copy of the warrant, known as the execution copy, or by the use of a copy of the execution copy, including a copy transmitted by facsimile machine or other means of electronic communication.

history.raw: S. 57(8) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 4(2).

nodes.text: The execution copy of a warrant must be in writing and, subject to subsection (1A), must be signed or otherwise authenticated by the person issuing it.

history.raw: S. 57(9) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 4(3).

nodes.heading: Warrants to arrest issued under Evidence Act 2008
nodes.text: The provisions of this Division relating to warrants to arrest extend and apply to a warrant to arrest issued under section 194 of the Evidence Act 2008 except as otherwise provided in this Division.

history.raw: S. 57A inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.4).

nodes.text: A warrant issued by a registrar, judicial registrar, magistrate or bail justice may be recalled and cancelled by2—

history.raw: S. 58(1) amended by No. 33/2018 s. 51(a).

nodes.text: that registrar, judicial registrar, magistrate or bail justice; or

history.raw: S. 58(1)(a) amended by No. 33/2018 s. 51(b).

nodes.text: if issued by a judicial registrar, any other judicial registrar; or

history.raw: S. 58(1)(ab) inserted by No. 17/2023 s. 37.

nodes.text: if issued by a registrar, the registrar for the time being at the venue of the Court at which it was issued or, except in the case of an enforcement warrant issued under the Fines Reform Act 2014, any other registrar; or

history.raw: S. 58(1)(b) amended by Nos 44/1997 s. 29, 12/2006 s. 169(d), substituted by No. 47/2014 s. 272(1).

nodes.text: a magistrate.
If a warrant has been recalled and cancelled under subsection (1), a fresh warrant may be issued for the same purpose as that for which the recalled warrant was issued.

history.raw: S. 58(1A) inserted by No. 70/1996 s. 4.

nodes.text: A warrant to imprison or detain in a youth justice centre for non-payment of a fine (whether issued before or after the commencement of this section) is null and void if it has not been executed within the period of 5 years after a warrant of that type was first issued against the person named in the warrant for the purpose specified in the warrant3,4,5.

If a warrant referred to in subsection (2) becomes null and void under that subsection, the fine in respect of which it was issued, together with any associated fees and costs, ceases to be enforceable or recoverable if no part of the fine had been paid before the date on which the warrant became null and void.

history.raw: S. 58(2A) inserted by No. 70/1996 s. 5(2).

nodes.text: Nothing in subsection (2) or (2A) prevents the issue, with the leave of the Court, of a fresh warrant for the same purpose as that for which a warrant that has become null and void under subsection (2) was issued6.

Despite subsection (2), if under subsection (3) a fresh warrant is issued, the fine in respect of which it was issued, together with any associated fees and costs, again becomes enforceable or recoverable as if there had been no cessation.

history.raw: S. 58(4) inserted by No. 70/1996 s. 5(4).

nodes.text: If the execution copy of a warrant issued by a registrar, judicial registrar, magistrate or bail justice is lost or destroyed before it is executed, a registrar, judicial registrar or magistrate may issue a duplicate execution copy if satisfied by evidence on oath or affirmation or by affidavit of the loss or destruction of the execution copy of the warrant.
A duplicate execution copy must bear on its face the word "Duplicate" and may be executed in all respects as if it were the execution copy of the warrant.
When a duplicate execution copy of a warrant is issued, the execution copy of the warrant becomes null and void and must, if located, be returned to the principal registrar.

If a person is in a prison, a police gaol or a youth justice centre in accordance with a warrant which has been executed, or having been released on parole from a prison, a police gaol or a youth justice centre is still under sentence, and the execution copy of the warrant is lost or destroyed, a registrar, judicial registrar or magistrate may issue a duplicate execution copy if satisfied by evidence on oath or affirmation or by affidavit of the loss or destruction of the execution copy.

A duplicate execution copy issued under subsection (4) is sufficient authority for the person in whose legal custody the person is, or into whose legal custody the person is delivered, to keep the person in the prison, police gaol or youth justice centre until the end of the term specified in the warrant.

nodes.heading: Effect of defect or error in certain warrants

nodes.text: A warrant to imprison, a warrant to detain in a youth justice centre, a remand warrant, a warrant to seize property or an enforcement warrant7 is not void only because of a defect or error in it if there is a valid order supporting it.
A person acting under a warrant to seize property or an enforcement warrant8 is not to be taken to be a trespasser from the beginning only because of a defect or error in it.

history.raw: S. 61(4) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.30).
Note to s. 61 inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.6).

nodes.text: A warrant to arrest in the first instance may be issued—

history.raw: S. 61(1)(a) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.29).
S. 61(1)(b) repealed by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.5).

nodes.text: as authorised by any other Act.

history.raw: S. 61(5)(c) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.31).

nodes.text: An application for a warrant to arrest in the first instance must be supported by evidence on oath or affirmation or by affidavit.

history.raw: S. 61(2) amended by No. 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 81.1).

nodes.text: An affidavit supporting an application for a warrant to arrest in the first instance may be a copy of an affidavit transmitted by facsimile machine or other means of electronic communication.

history.raw: S. 61(3) amended by No. 3/2016 s. 5.

nodes.text: A warrant to arrest other than in the first instance may be issued—

history.raw: S. 61(5)(a) repealed by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.31).
S. 61(5)(b) repealed by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.5).

nodes.text: as authorised by this or any other Act.
A warrant to arrest other than in the first instance must include a statement of the reason for issuing the warrant.
Section 194 of the Evidence Act 2008 provides for issuing warrants to arrest a witness who fails to appear.
The person issuing a warrant to arrest against any person may endorse the warrant with a direction that that person must on arrest be released on bail as specified in the endorsement.

An endorsement under subsection (1) must fix the amounts in which the principal and the bail guarantors, if any, are to be bound and the amount of any money or the value of any security to be deposited.
This section does not apply in respect of a warrant authorised to be issued under section 194 of the Evidence Act 2008.

history.raw: S. 62(3) inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.7).

nodes.heading: Persons to whom warrant to arrest may be directed

nodes.text: A warrant to arrest may be directed to—
a named police officer; or

history.raw: S. 63(1)(a) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.2(a)(i)).

nodes.text: generally all police officers; or

history.raw: S. 63(1)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.2(a)(ii)).

nodes.text: any other person authorised by law to execute a warrant to arrest.
A warrant to arrest directed to a named police officer may be executed by any police officer.

history.raw: S. 63(2) substituted by No. 43/2011 s. 35, amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.2(b)), substituted by No. 39/2019 s. 14(1).

nodes.text: A warrant to arrest directed to a named police officer or to generally all police officers may be executed by any protective services officer.

history.raw: S. 63(2A) inserted by No. 39/2019 s. 14(1).

nodes.text: If a protective services officer arrests a person under subsection (2A), the protective services officer must hand the person into the custody of a police officer as soon as practicable after the person is arrested.

history.raw: S. 63(3) inserted by No, 43/2011 s. 35, amended by Nos 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.2(b)), 39/2019 s. 14(2).

nodes.heading: Authority conferred by warrant to arrest

nodes.text: A warrant to arrest authorises the person to whom it is directed—
to break, enter and search any place where the person named or described in the warrant is suspected to be; and

history.raw: S. 64(2)(a) amended by No. 49/1990 s. 5(a).

nodes.text: to arrest the person named or described in the warrant.
The person to whom a warrant to arrest is directed must cause the person named or described in the warrant when arrested—

history.raw: Note to s. 64(2) inserted by No. 26/2017 s. 24(1).

nodes.text: to be brought before a bail justice or the Court within a reasonable time of being arrested to be dealt with according to law; or
to be released on bail in accordance with the endorsement on the warrant.
Section 10A or 12 of the Bail Act 1977 applies on a person being brought before a bail justice or the Court at the expiration of the reasonable time referred to in subsection (2)(a).
A person arrested on a warrant to arrest may be discharged from custody on bail in accordance with the Bail Act 1977.
In determining what constitutes a reasonable time for the purposes of subsection (2)(a) the matters specified in section 464A(4) of the Crimes Act 1958 may be considered.

history.raw: S. 64(4) inserted by No. 49/1990 s. 5(b).

nodes.text: If a person is brought before a bail justice or the Court in accordance with subsection (2)(a), the bail justice or the Court is not bound by the endorsement on the warrant when determining any matter in relation to bail.

history.raw: S. 64(4A) inserted by No. 70/2010 s. 27(1).

nodes.text: Subsections (2), (3), (4) and (4A) do not apply in respect of a warrant authorised to be issued under section 194 of the Evidence Act 2008.

history.raw: S. 64(5) inserted by No. 69/2009 s. 54(Sch. Pt 1 item 34.8), amended by No. 70/2010 s. 27(2).

nodes.heading: Arrest of person against whom warrant to arrest is issued

nodes.text: If a warrant to arrest a person who is an accused to a charge has been issued, any police officer, or any protective services officer on duty at a designated place, may arrest the person although the execution copy of the warrant is not at the time in the police officer's or protective services officer's possession.

If a protective services officer arrests a person under subsection (1), the protective services officer must hand the person into the custody of a police officer as soon as practicable after the person is arrested.

history.raw: S. 65(1A) inserted by No. 43/2011 s. 36(2), amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 101.3(b)).

nodes.text: A protective services officer may only exercise the power to arrest under this section in relation to a person who is at, or in the vicinity of, a designated place.

history.raw: S. 65(1B) inserted by No. 45/2017 s. 55.

nodes.text: On the arrest of a person under subsection (1) by a police officer or on the handing of a person arrested by a protective services officer into the custody of a police officer under subsection (1A), the police officer must bring the person arrested before a bail justice or the Court within a reasonable time of being arrested or handed into the custody of the police officer (as the case may be) and the bail justice or the Court may—
if a fresh charge-sheet is filed to the effect of the offence or matter alleged in the warrant—

history.raw: S. 65(2)(a) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.33).

nodes.text: permit the person to go at large; or
admit the person to bail; or
in the case of the Court, hear and determine the proceeding for the offence; or
if a fresh charge-sheet is not filed to the effect of the offence or matter alleged in the warrant—

history.raw: S. 65(2)(b) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.33).

nodes.text: permit the person to go at large; or
admit the person to bail; or
remand the person in custody for a reasonable time pending execution of the warrant.

If a person has been arrested under subsection (1) and has been remanded in custody pending execution of the warrant and the warrant is not executed within a reasonable time, the Court must discharge the person from custody.
If a warrant is executed by use of a copy other than the execution copy, the Court must—
if satisfied that the copy is a true copy of the execution copy—
proceed as if the person had been arrested on the execution copy; and
order that the execution copy be returned to the principal registrar; or
if not so satisfied, discharge the person from custody.

If a warrant is not executed and a fresh charge-sheet charging the offence alleged in the warrant is filed, the warrant is deemed to be void and of no effect and the Court must order its return to the principal registrar.

history.raw: S. 65(5) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 82.34).

nodes.text: In determining what constitutes a reasonable time for the purposes of subsection (2) the matters specified in section 464A(4) of the Crimes Act 1958 may be considered.

nodes.text: A warrant to imprison may be issued if—
the Court orders that a person be sentenced to a term of imprisonment; or
the Court orders that a person be sentenced to a term of imprisonment in default of payment of a fine or of any instalment under an instalment order; or
authorised by any other Act.

nodes.text: A warrant to imprison—

directs and authorises the person to whom it is directed to take and safely convey the person named in the warrant—and there to deliver the person to the officer in charge of the prison or police gaol; and

if the warrant is issued under section 68(b), either to a prison or a police gaol;

nodes.heading: Reduction of imprisonment by payment of portion of fine

nodes.text: If before the issue of a warrant to imprison for non-payment of a fine, it appears to the person issuing the warrant that part of the fine has been paid—
the reduction in the amount of the fine payable must be stated in the warrant to imprison; and

the term for which the person fined may be imprisoned must be reduced by the number of days bearing as nearly as possible the same proportion to the total number of days in the term as the amount paid bears to the whole amount of the fine.
Subsection (1) applies despite any provision (except section 26) of the Imprisonment of Fraudulent Debtors Act 1958 to the contrary.

If after the issue but before the execution of a warrant to imprison for non-payment of a fine, it appears to the Court that part of the fine has been paid, the Court must—in accordance with subsection (1).
amend the warrant; and
recall the execution copy of the warrant and amend it—

Despite any provision (except section 26) of the Imprisonment of Fraudulent Debtors Act 1958 to the contrary or anything in any warrant to imprison, if a person is imprisoned for non-payment of a fine—
the whole or any part of the fine may be paid by or on behalf of that person to the officer in charge of the prison or police gaol in which that person is detained; and
the officer in charge must receive the payment and forward it without delay to the principal registrar.
If—is paid to the officer in charge of the prison or police gaol by or on behalf of the person imprisoned, the person imprisoned must be discharged if he or she is in custody for no other matter.
the whole amount of the fine; or
the amount remaining to be paid—
If part of the fine is paid to the officer in charge of the prison or police gaol by or on behalf of the person imprisoned—
the term of imprisonment for non-payment of the fine must be reduced having regard to the formula set out in subsection (1)(b); and
the officer in charge must—
amend the execution copy of the warrant; and
receive the payment and forward it without delay to the principal registrar; and
at the end of the reduced term, the person imprisoned must be discharged if he or she is in custody for no other matter.

nodes.heading: Provisions extend to detention in youth justice centre
nodes.text: If a person is directed under Subdivision (4) of Division 2 of Part 3 of the Sentencing Act 1991 or under the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005 to be detained in a youth justice centre or a youth residential centre, the provisions of this Subdivision and of any regulations with respect to warrants to imprison extend and apply, with any necessary modifications, with respect to the issue and execution of a warrant to detain in a youth justice centre or a youth residential centre and with respect to any matter arising out of any such detention.

nodes.text: A warrant to seize property directs and authorises the person to whom it is directed—
to seize the personal property of the person named or described in the warrant; and
if the sums named in the warrant together with all lawful costs of execution are not paid, to sell the personal property seized.

A search warrant authorises the person to whom it is directed—

to bring the article, thing or material before the Court so that the matter may be dealt with according to law; and

the fine is payable—

nodes.text: means another State or a Territory of the Commonwealth that is declared by proclamation under this section to be a reciprocating State or Territory.

The Governor in Council may, subject to subsection (3), declare another State or a Territory of the Commonwealth to be a reciprocating State or Territory for the purposes of the enforcement against a body corporate in Victoria of a fine payable under an order of a court having summary jurisdiction in the other State or in the Territory.

A State or Territory the subject of a proclamation under subsection (2) must have laws providing for enforcement against a body corporate in that State or Territory of a fine payable under an order of the Magistrates' Court or other court having summary jurisdiction in Victoria.

The Governor in Council may by proclamation declare a court having summary jurisdiction in a reciprocating State or Territory to be a reciprocating court for the purposes of the enforcement against a body corporate in Victoria of a fine payable under a conviction or order of that court.

For the purposes of subsection (4) a court may be declared singly or in conjunction with another or others by such description or class or by means of any reference that the Governor in Council thinks fit.

If, under an order of a reciprocating court made in the exercise of its summary jurisdiction—the registrar must register the order in the Magistrates' Court by filing in the Court a certified copy of the order and must note the date of registration on the copy.
a fine is payable by a body corporate having or appearing to have property in Victoria; and

a registrar of the Magistrates' Court at a venue at or near to a place where the body corporate has or appears to have property, receives a request in writing from a registrar or other corresponding officer of the reciprocating court for the enforcement of the order accompanied by—
a certified copy of the order; and
a certificate signed by the registrar or corresponding officer making the request certifying the amount of the fine outstanding under the order—

the order is deemed to be an order of the Magistrates' Court requiring payment by the body corporate of the amount of the fine referred to in the certificate under subsection (6) as outstanding; and
the registrar may issue a warrant to seize property of the body corporate for the purpose of recovering the amount of the fine; and

the warrant issued under paragraph (b) is deemed to be a warrant to seize property issued under this Act and the provisions of this Act, with any necessary modifications, apply and extend to the enforcement of that warrant.

If the registrar receives, after the request for the enforcement of the order, a notification from the registrar or other corresponding officer of the reciprocating court of payment by or on behalf of the body corporate of the whole or part of the outstanding fine, the registrar must—
note the particulars of the payment on the certified copy of the order filed in the Court; and
arrange for the return of the warrant issued under subsection (7)(b), if it is unexecuted; and
if the fine—
has been paid in full, withdraw the warrant; or

The registrar of the Magistrates' Court must remit to the registrar or other corresponding officer of the reciprocating court which made the order any sum of money received in satisfaction of the whole or part of a fine payable under an order enforced under subsection (7).

Any sum of money paid to or received by a registrar of the Magistrates' Court from a reciprocating court in satisfaction of the whole or part of a fine payable under an order of the Magistrates' Court enforced by the reciprocating court must be paid to or received by and applied by the registrar as if the sum had been paid to the registrar by the body corporate by which the fine was payable.
